Silent Hill 2 - i właściwie cała ta seria - to wyjątkowe doświadczenie w świecie gier. Gdy grałem w oryginał w czasach szkolnych, czułem beznadziejność, głęboki smutek i strach... prawdziwe przerażenie. Dla mnie była to najstraszniejsza gra w historii - nie przez jump scare’y, ale przez duszącą atmosferę. Minęło dwadzieścia lat i nic się nie zmieniło.  Remake przygniata tą samą atmosferą od początku do końca co oryginalne SH 2. Gra wspierana jest przez legendarną ścieżką dźwiękową Akiry Yamaoki. To jedyny tytuł, w którym naprawdę czujesz się niekomfortowo będąc w jego świecie. Chcesz go wyłączyć, uciec - i właśnie w tym Blooberzy odnieśli OGROMNY sukces.  Tak, mamy dziś wiele świetnych survival horrorów — Alan Wake, seria Resident Evil czy The Evil Within - ale tylko w Silent Hill 2 poczujesz coś takiego. I dlatego ta gra pozostaje jedyna w swoim rodzaju.  Wyjątkowa jest też fabuła — tak osobista, tak intymna dla każdego z bohaterów: Jamesa, Angeli, Eddiego. Jeśli kochasz narracje bogate w psychologiczną głębię, to jest gra dla ciebie.  A dla tych, którzy grali w oryginał, Bloober przygotował niespodzianki: Glimpses of the Past, czyli nawiązania do konkretnych momentów, scen czy przedmiotów z pierwowzoru, oraz dwa zupełnie nowe zakończenia. Oba są godne oryginału, a jedno z nich jest tak mocne, że wywołuje ciarki - i naprawdę można pomyśleć: „Tak, to może być najlepsze zakończenie dla Jamesa”.  Niezapomniana gra. Wyjątkowy survival horror. Doświadczenie jedyne w swoim rodzaju, które wchodzi pod skórę i nie pozwala o sobie zapomnieć.  Arcydzieło.
Превосходная игра! Одна из лучших игр в которые я играл в этом году, рекомендую всем ознакомиться как с игрой так с историей.

Curiosamente este es uno de eso juegos que te hace sufrir tanto que te sientes vivo,  No hay nada más doloroso que vivir junto al protagonista, acompañar sus suspiros en pleno silencio y dolor sin tener ni la ligera idea de la gravedad del asunto, del peso que cargaba, para al final, desmantelar la caja de los secretos y comenzar a hilar las piezas.   No se trata de una historia en el que el protagonista sea bueno o malo, nadie es totalmente bueno o malo aquí, todo es un equilibrio lleno de complejidades junto a la culpa y arrepentimiento de James, cada escenario se siente como un viaje en el interior de su mente, alborotada, sucia, podrida, llena de ilusiones.   Todos tienen sus razones, pero al final eres tú quien decide como llevar el peso del pecado en tus espaldas.

Easily one of the best horror games I've played in a while. The pace, the game loop, graphics, sound, story and environments. It's the right amount of scary without being stressful. Not too forgiving with resources, yet generous enough. Puzzles are fun. Fighting mechanics are intuitive.  I've been a fan of horror games since the first Resident Evil came out. But for some reason I just could not get into Silent Hill, despite being such a popular franchise. And it was not because I didn't want it, but because circumstances never let it happen.  It was until the PS3 era when I first got to play one: Silent Hill Homecoming. While that game is universally hated, it was my first Silent Hill and I found it to be an amazing horror game. The only negatives I could find was the bad controls and overall performance, which was not very good.  I don't feel that this game is that different in terms of content, but just the fact that it is very well polished and the graphics have been improved, make it a much more enjoyable experience.  I don't have much to say in terms of lore and such because this is my second Silent Hill, and my first mainline title. Compared to the only Silent Hill I've played before, it feels like it follows the same formula (I know I'll get destroyed by SH fans for saying this).  I never expected to enjoy it as much as I have. I don't think I can find any negatives about this game. Even performance has been solid. No crashes, stuttering, FPS dips, etc. Maxed out graphics, 1440p, RT on, 120fps. And it plays great with a generic Xbox One controller.

Simplesmente incrível.  SILENT HILL 2 é para mim o absoluto ápice dos Survivor Horror: ambientação magnífica, inimigos memoráveis, seções memoráveis, puzzles interessantes, exploração satisfatória e entre outros inúmeros pontos positivos a serem mencionados a respeito desse jogo.  A trama desse jogo dispensa comentários, desde o lançamento do jogo original a história desse jogo é debatida e comentada, e nesse remake conseguiram trazer essa trama pra modernidade de uma maneira extremamente competente.  James Sunderland é pra mim possivelmente o personagem mais bem escrito nos jogos, é impressionante o que foi feito com esse personagem em apenas 16 horas. Basicamente TUDO no jogo comunica algo sobre esse personagem, a maneira como ele pensa, age ou o que ele sente.   Através de cutscenes, cenários, cartas e até mesmo puzzles nós entendemos mais desse personagem magnífico.  TRILHA SONORA [b] IMPECÁVEL[/b], disparado a melhor trilha sonora dentre todos os jogos que já joguei, cada música transmite exatamente o que a sua respectiva cena/personagem transmite.   É refrescante ver um jogo com um personagem realmente falho, com uma personalidade complexa o suficiente para possibilitar diversas interpretações para cada um que joga esse jogo.  A experiência de jogar esse jogo mais algumas vezes e platinar foi extremamente divertida para mim, por mais que eu acredite que esse jogo não tem lá um grande fator de rejogabilidade.  A respeito de defeitos, é fácil argumentar que o preço do jogo é altíssimo pra quantidade de conteúdo que ele proporciona (R$ 350,00 full-price ou R$200,00 na promoção no momento em que estou escrevendo essa análise), mas se você gosta desse gênero e dessa saga eu diria que vale a pena, ainda mais em promoção.  Além do preço, é inegável o dano causado pelo UE5 nesse jogo, que apesar de deixar o jogo com gráficos absurdos de lindos, causa stutter até em configurações mais high-end.  Apesar desses problemas esse jogo vale muito a pena pra qualquer amante do gênero e principalmente da franquia.  11/10.

Den ersten Durchlauf kann man hier angucken: https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL9opVmvUmcDJ3M2iFlrlBA5nqc9RNw03E  Was soll ich sagen? Das ist der absolut beste Silent Hill Teil überhaupt. Das Remake macht das Original nochmals um sovieles besser. Hatte damals alle 7 Enden geholt, weil schon damals das Spiel eine Bombe war. Die Story und Gebiete wurden sinnvoll erweitert und vor allem nochmal um ein vielfaches emotionaler gemacht.  Die Performance geht vollkommen in Ordnung. Ohne Streaming gehen 4K max Settings bei Balanced DLSS. Mit Stream ist 4K max Settings und Ultra Performance DLSS möglich. Frame Generation habe ich nicht verwendet, da es nur absoluten Grafikmüll auf den Bildschirm knallt. Was ich für ein Problem hatte, selbst wenn ich den Desktop auf 1440p und 60 FPS begrenze, läuft das Spiel weiterhin auf den Bildschirmspecs von 4K und 120 FPS. Selbst VSync und auch 60 FPS In-Game-Limiter helfen hier nicht. Das Sounddesign sucht absolut seines gleichen, habe so einen bombastischen 3D-Sound mit Kopfhörern noch nie gehört. Auch das Redesign der Charaktere gefällt mir sehr, da diese nun viel besser zu den Charakteren passt. Die Atmosphäre ist hier auf dauerhaften Höchstniveau, was aber auch für einige zu belastend sein kann. Es ist ein Psychological Horror und das OHNE Kompromisse. Eine klare Warnung muss ich allerdings geben! Gerade die Triggerthemen können in diesen Spiel einen ganz schön belasten und runterziehen, da sie eben so emotional rüber gebracht werden, egal ob nun in Textform oder Bildlich!!! Ich habe für meinen ersten Run ca. 20 Stunden gebraucht, habe aber auch jeden Winkel erkundet. Angenehm ist auch das es ein neues Ende gibt und das freischalten der Enden überarbeitet wurde.  Kann das Spiel absolut jeden empfehlen der psychisch belastbar ist. Am sonsten müsst ihr euch fragen ob Themen wie [spoiler]Vergewaltigung, Selbstverletzung, Häusliche Gewalt, Mobbing, Suizid[/spoiler] nicht zuviel sind.

Sin temor puedo decir que es uno de los remakes más logrados que han sacado de franquicias con ya varios años desde su salida. Silent Hill 2 logra una atmosfera de terror y soledad constantes a lo largo de lo que avanzas en el juego y se agradece que añadieran finales adicionales a los cuales no estaban en el juego original. Aún así, por contenido post-game, faltan armas desbloqueables, que solo tengas la motosierra que mata de un one hit a la mayoria de enemigos, hace que sea más rapido la experiencia de desbloquear coleccionables y finales extra pero con 2 o 3 armas diferentes dependiendo de los desafios, hubiera sido todavia más gratificante volverte a pasar el juego. A día de hoy, 5 de octubre del 2025, el rendimiento en PC esta mejor logrado, aunque desgraciadamente el motor de UE5 genera stuttering en varias partes del juego que te pueden llegar a sacar un poco de la experiencia. Algunos mods arreglan gran parte de ese problema pero no lo eliminan por completo, asi que vete preparado, ya que teniendo un equipo de gama alta o gama baja, será medianamente la misma experiencia jugable. Recomiendo el juego tal vez no a precio completo por ese problema en especifico, no se si requieran más optimizaciones pero a estas fechas dudo que reciba más actualizaciones y menos la edición deluxe el cual solo libera trajes extras para James. Sin dudas, obviando todo lo anterior, la atmosfera, el OST, el estilo visual y la historia en general, hacen que este juego sea una gran puerta de entrada a nuevos jugadores y a veteranos que quieran revivir la historia de este gran juego (teniendo en cuenta que SH2 no sigue precisamente la continuidad de SH1 y SH3, sino que es su propia cosa aparte).

Genuinely the best survival horror game in since probably re7 imo. The game is gorgeous with RT on and the sound design might be the best in a horror game i've played. Be warned, its not a "fun" story nor is it really a fun game to play.   Its not a jump scare heavy type of game in the vein of visage or similar but instead it simply uses dread & suspense that doesnt go away, from the apartment section to the hospital(and beyond) it simply never really gives you a time to breath.  The combat is mostly ok with a similar feeling to RE2 remake but just alot slower in general, James isnt really the quickest character to move around or hit things with. There's not alot of enemy variation either but i think its more ok than usual since combat isnt constant(maybe except for the prison area) and while i enjoyed the combat it does drag on a bit towards the end. Healing items & ammunition might be given a bit to often tbh, i think i had around 30 heals throughout the last areas to the end of the game which made some areas & bosses very trivial and easy to fight through.  I think James is my favourite game protagonist in a long time, he is not perfect in the slightest but you cant help but you cant help but to feel sorry for the dude, he is just depressed as hell and is not having a good time throughout the game.   The only real downside is the length, i finished the game in about 14.5 hours which could have and should have been cut down a few hours(specially parts of the hospital & the labyrinth). Those areas that drag on are not bad at all but just feels a bit boring to go  through after a while(thinking of the otherworld hospital here etc).  Its a 9/10 for me and a actual must play for most people, even tho its a scary game i think the story and its themes are things people very much should experience and also talk about.

We need more horror games tackling themes of mental health. Silent Hill 2 isn't just an unsettling game, it's an emotional one. It's not afraid of diving into the darkest parts of the human psyche, and I felt some of these themes were something that I (and most likely others) have experienced ourselves.  The atmosphere is oppressive and suffocating, the ambience and immersion is some of the best I've experienced in a video game. This is a slow-paced game where you soak everything in and explore as much you can, with the game rewarding you for it. There are multiple endings that are entirely determined by [i]how[/i] you play. I won't get much into it, but [i]everything[/i] you do will decide which ending path you're headed towards, so keep that in mind.  The combat is satisfying and does its job. My most used weapon was a steel pipe (I prefer melee combat) and whacking down the monsters never got old. The enemies were grotesque, with the boss designs taking everything to a horrifyingly new level. I guess my only criticism is that I felt the game was a bit [i]too[/i] generous with the ammo and health supply (I like to struggle and suffer), but it doesn't take away from the game at all.  The music is just amazing. We all know how good Akira Yamaoka is at this point, I'll just leave it at that.  The voice acting is phenomenal. Luke Roberts not getting the recognition he deserved for his portrayal of James is a genuine crime. You could hear the uncertainty, hurt, confusion, frustration, trauma, in every line - it just felt [i]real[/i], with one of the endings being an all-time performance in a video game.  Anyways, I think I've gone on for long enough. I absolutely love this game - so much so that I'm planning to go for all endings and try to achieve 100%. I have Silent Hill f ready to play once I'm done and I can't wait. I'm glad Silent Hill has had a resurgence and I'm hoping they can maintain this level of quality for future games (I can't wait for the Silent Hill 1 remake).  Play this game.

„Ein Albtraum, schön wie eine schlechte Erinnerung.“  [b]Atmosphäre & Grafik[/b]  Der erste Eindruck: Silent Hill war nie schöner und gleichzeitig nie beängstigender. Bloober Team nutzt Unreal Engine 5, und das zahlt sich aus. Die Stadt, das Nebelspiel, Schatten und Licht, alles wirkt lebendiger, dreckiger, greifbarer. Der Nebel fühlt sich nicht mehr wie eine Maske an, hinter der Texturen versteckt sind, sondern wie eine Präsenz – etwas, das wabert, etwas, das dich umgibt, dich verfolgt.   Auch Charaktere und Monster haben viel mehr Details: Falten, Dreck, Verzerrungen, herunterhängende Textilien – all das trägt dazu bei, dass der Horror nicht nur in jump scares passiert, sondern in jedem Schritt, jedem Blick in eine menschenleere Gasse.   Sound & Musik sind – wie in Silent Hill üblich – essenziell. Aki­ra Yamaoka kehrt zurück, Themen werden neu interpretiert, Soundeffekte sind subtiler und gruseliger. Zum ersten Mal hörst du Geräusche, die dich wirklich nervös machen – ein Knarzen, Flüstern, Schritte weit weg, dann näher. Das Radio, das Summen, das Knistern – manchmal wünscht man sich Ohrstöpsel, aber gleichzeitig will man nichts verpassen, weil jeder Ton Bedeutung haben kann.   [b]Gameplay & Perspektive[/b]  Eine der größten Änderungen: Die Kamera. Weg mit den fixen Kamerawinkeln des Originals – das Remake setzt auf Over-the-Shoulder. Das bringt Vor- und Nachteile:  Vorteile: Du spürst James‘ Angst näher. Du siehst Monster aus seiner Perspektive – und das macht manches Begegnung intensiver. Die Steuerung bei Kämpfen wirkt moderner, Bewegungen sind flüssiger, Ausweichmanöver sind sinnvoller geworden.   Nachteile: Manche der klassischen fixen Blickwinkel fehlen fehlert. Die cinematografische Wirkung mancher Szenen ist nicht mehr ganz dieselbe; einige Momente verlieren etwas von ihrer ikonischen Bildkomposition. Für Puristen sind das Augenblicke des Nostalgieverlusts.   Auch die Gegnertypen und Kämpfe wurden angepasst: schneller, aggressiver, anspruchsvoller. Begegnungen sind weniger berechenbar. Rätsel und Levels sind oft vertraut, aber es gibt neue Bereiche und Wege, die vorher nicht zugänglich waren, sowie Änderungen bei Bosskämpfen und Begegnungen, die dem Remake frische Spannung verleihen.   [b]Story & Identität[/b]  Hier bleibt das Herz von Silent Hill 2 intakt: James Sunderland, seine Suche nach Mary, die Schuld, die Trauer, das Unausgesprochene. Die Erzählung funktioniert weiterhin stark, gerade weil viele Dialoge, viele Schlüsselthemen und symbolischen Elemente übernommen wurden.   Dennoch: Wer tief mit dem Original verwachsen ist, merkt Änderungen. Manche Szenen wurden umgestaltet, manche Begegnungen gestreckt oder neu inszeniert, und gelegentlich fühlt sich der Rhythmus anders an – weniger gedrosselt, mehr Druck. Die Fülle der neuen Inhalte wirkt zum Teil wie Erweiterung, zum Teil wie Gewicht, das dem Spiel die letzte ambivalente Eleganz nimmt.   [b]Kritikpunkte & Schwächen[/b]  Pacing: Einige Passagen fühlen sich gestreckt an. Was im Original funktionierte als Raum zum Atmen zwischen den Schrecken, wirkt hier manchmal wie ‚Luft holen ohne Ziel‘.   Kampfgefühl: Obwohl moderner, stören noch hin und wieder ungünstige Kamerawinkel oder Animationen. Gerade wenn Gegner plötzlich aus dem Nebel auftauchen, wird klar, dass Update nötig war – aber nicht überall gelingt der Spagat zwischen alter Tragik und neuer Spielbarkeit.   Technik: Auf manchen Plattformen gibt es Berichte über Performance-Probleme, Schwankungen bei Framerate, teilweise Ruckler oder technische Macken. Nicht extrem spielzerstörend, aber sie reißen gelegentlich aus dem Horror-Tunnel heraus.   [b]Fazit[/b]  Silent Hill 2 Remake ist kein perfektes Remake. Aber es ist eine beeindruckende und mutige Neuinterpretation eines Horror-Klassikers. Wer das Original liebt, wird hier viel Wiedererkennung finden – und auch neue Momente, die überraschen. Wer vorher noch kein Silent Hill gespielt hat, bekommt ein atmosphärisch starkes Horror-Erlebnis, das sowohl emotional als auch optisch überzeugt.  Ich würde dem Remake [b]8,5 / 10[/b] geben – für die Atmosphäre, die Liebe zum Detail, die gelungenen Modernisierungen. Abzüge gibt’s für das etwas veränderte Tempo und ein paar technische Schwächen. Aber insgesamt: Pflicht für Fans, sehr attraktiv für Genre-Einsteiger.  https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=r9TmIwchqfM

An absolutely legitimate immortalization of legends.  For me, as for many, the remake is the first part of Silent Hill. It definitely has its own beauty, especially in the way it plays with light.  The gameplay is generally within the bounds of the genre: loot things, solve puzzles, don't die. There are interesting elements such as optional interaction with the radio, which works as a locator.   The plot is definitely the strong point of this part. Since I didn't play the original, I followed the narrative closely throughout the game, and the plot is the only thing that makes you want to make your way through this world. Everything works well together and harmonizes.  I can't compare it to the original, I can't judge, I just know that the games are quite different. And I wouldn't want to. I just want to say that remakes like this grab your attention and make such works immortal.   Sincere thanks to the team for the experience. If this story is re-released in a different package with technological advances, I'll be only glad.

Never ever have i played a better game in the horror genre than Silent Hill 2 (Remake). The psychological displeasure of this game is underlined with an atmosphere like no other. There are very few jumpscares, but the ones that actually are in the game are phenomenal. Because of this circumstance you always have to stay sharp and concentrated. But the true fact that makes this game so interesting is its unmatched ambient. Fog, noises, the people you meet, the town itself. You always ask yourself - "whats even happening here?" until the plot gets revealed and you do your own research afterwards, which is absolutely mindblowing once you realize the true nature of all the protagonists.  The little details are unmatched for this genre. Facial expressions, dialogue hints, metaphors - you name it. After finishing the game I was still very invested and to this day still I occasionally read lore or watch videos about the true meaning of many scenes, enemies, the main characters etc. even tho I finished the game nearly a year ago.  Combat is intense and very fair. It can feel slow at certain times, but thats exactly why fighting is so pleasurable. The enemies are terrifying, boss battles are insanely well done with great variety of attack-patterns. Puzzles are extremely smart designed. Pacing is phenomenal. The story is one of the best written stories not only in the gaming-world, but in fiction/theater/movies in general and i truly mean it.  I will 100% replay this and get a physical copy for my PS5 too.  This is in my Top 5 Games of all time, if not even higher.  Must play.  10/10

[h1]Обратная сторона медали[/h1]  Я пропустил оригинал второй части Тихих Холмов, как большинство других шедевров времен 1-2 плейстейшн. Игры в моей семье были под частичным запретом, поэтому играл я только на компьютере и в основном в стратегии, что, конечно, не плохо, но распробовать хорроры, которые в итоге стали моим любимым жанром я тогда не смог. Да и плейстейшна у меня никогда не было. Сейчас, понимать это крайне обидно, потому что впечатления уже не те и, чего греха таить, не смотря на обновленную графику, структура игры устарела. Враги-губки, куча бектреккинга, загадки, простые, но требующие тыкаться в каждую закрытую дверь по пути - все это не лучшее времяпрепровождение и под конец игра начинает серьезно душить всем этим. Но... какая же тут шикарная подача сюжета.  [h2]Учите мат-часть[/h2]  В процессе игры я начал подмечать за собой любопытство по отношению к лору происходящего. Произошло это из двух факторов - необычный дизайн врагов и окружения, плюс, куча недосказанностей, открывающих пространство для интерпретаций. Все эти странный фотографии подписанные кем-то совершенно безумным, странные стишки с узнаваемыми тропами из европейских средневековых сказок, но при этом оформленные в гротескной, искаженной манере. Не знаю, понял бы я все происходящее без помощи вики, но сам факт существования такой вики и того что я в нее зашел уже говорит о многом. Словом, сюжет и его подача - потрясающие. А концовка (знаю, их много, я прошел на базовую) - очень трогательная и даже затронула мои личные чувства (нет, у меня нет мертвой жены).  [h2]О густоте тумана[/h2]  Визуал - прекрасный. Туман объемный, водичка блестит лучами, а на лице Джеймса видна каждая пора. При желании можно придраться к волосам и отдельным моделям, порезанным в угоду неплохой оптимизации и небольшого размера игры (да-да, 30 с лишним гигов по нынешним меркам - не много). Музыка - тоже очень хорошая там - где это музыка. Эмбиент с ударами чем-то металлическим по батарее меня скорее раздражал. Из минусов - слегка корявая анимация лиц, но это придирки и на вскидку мне сложно вспомнить - где она лучше. Просто здесь это важно, поэтому и бросается в глаза.  [h2]На сколько велики глаза у страха[/h2]  А вот тут - вопрос спорный. На сколько эта игра страшная? В свое время я удивлялся с одноклассников, считающих Дум 3 - страшным. Выскакивающие из-за угла громозеки меня никогда особо не впечатляли. Куда сильнее я боялся неизвестности, таящейся в темноте. И отдельные уровни меня действительно пугали - например тюрьма. Но в общем и целом - нет. Эта игра не страшная. И финальная эмоция после ее прохождения - грусть, а не чувство освобождения, которое получаешь по окончании действительно классного хоррора. Плохо ли это? - На мой субъективный взгляд нет. Потому что лучше хорошая драма, чем посредственная страшилка. Hauntingly beautiful.  Silent Hill 2 is gorgeous in the most terrifying way possible. I mean, it is scary: the whole journey, guaranteed to be over 12 hours long on a first run, is a long, slow descent into the depths of a post-industrial hell made of rusted metal, bloodied cloth, deformed enemies, and non-euclidean geography. A sizeable portion of my enjoyment of this game lay in its aesthetics, and holy hell, did it deliver. Floors lead to empty voids, interior ceilings may or may not exist, Silent Hill itself turns inside-out and adopts the appearance of machinery's interiors, and claustrophobia reigns supreme. Whether in the [spoiler]normal town[/spoiler] and its desolate, sinister, isolating aura, or the [spoiler]Otherworld[/spoiler] and its oppressive, screeching, decaying premise, the modern visuals never failed to disappoint.  At the same time, Silent Hill 2 is a captivating sight to behold: the story is utterly captivating and compelling, and seeing James Sunderland's slog through his rotting iron purgatory, replete with guilt, punishment, and cruel metaphors, will be hard for me to forget. From Half-Life 2 to Resident Evil 4 to Spec Ops: The Line, I've always loved the long, nearly-unbroken journey across a vast space, learning more about the characters as they overcome greater trials, and SH2 is no exception. Never played the original, so I can't say how accurate or faithful it is, but it doesn't really matter that much to me. The underlying themes of [spoiler]guilt, trauma, and active repression of memories over an atrocious but darkly-understandable action in the face of watching a loved one slowly die with no hope for a cure[/spoiler] is a series off raw gut-punches, wrought with disturbing visual metaphors in the environmental, enemy, and atmospheric design.  The realistic aspects of Silent Hill 2 were well-received; the voice acting and dialogue stayed perfectly believable, and the acting itself was excellent throughout. Every character was memorable: James and Pyramid Head for obvious reasons, but Maria's, Eddie's, and Laura's performances gave the game a perfectly surreal and unsettling atmosphere. Combat isn't particularly hard if you're good at resource management, but on the hardest difficulty, it's not easy either. Preserving bullets and medical supplies is crucial, but if you're diligent with melee, saving up a few dozen bullets or so is entirely doable. They'll be needed during boss fights. Puzzles aren't hard either, but if they're not your thing, the experience of walking back and forth between rooms to find trinkets for hours won't be overly fun. This game is a masterpiece to me, though, and a gold-standard remake of a classic psychological horror game that's guaranteed to stick around in a player's brain for years.

Dieses Spiel ist absolut phänomenal. Ich habe es zwar erst vergleichsweise spät gespielt, allerdings bin ich absolut beeindruckt.  Ich bin eigentlich eher ein Angsthase, allerdings ist dieses Spiel so unfassbar fesselnd, dass ich davon nicht losgekommen bin. Ich hatte auch erst Angst, da ich mich schon ein wenig hab Spoilern lassen und durch meine "Road to Stillness" (das Stille Ende erreichen) auch nicht allzu sehr am "In Wasser"-Ende interessiert war.  Allerdings hat sich dies als Blödsinn herausgestellt. Ich habe das Spiel zu spielen absolut geliebt. Die Aufmachung, die Athmosphäre, die Musik und vor allem das eklig-widerliche Design haben für eine Spannung gesorgt, wie ich sie noch nie in einem Spiel gesehen habe. Das gepaart mit ein paar sehr düsteren, aber sehr realen Themen und den wunderbar gestalteten Enden hat das Ganze abgerundet. Selbst "In Wasser" konnte ich durch seine Tragik lieben lernen und ich bin sogar am Überlegen, ob ich "In Wasser" sogar geiler finde als Stille.  Die einzigen Dinge, welche mich am Spiel stören sind: - Manchmal wadern die Frisuren komisch rum, als würde sie gerade komisch vom Wind geschüttelt werden. Es wirkt allerdings nicht wie normales Haargekräusel vom Wind, sondern eher wie ein Animationsfehler. - In Stille kommt die Musik etwas zu früh und wird viel zu schnell düster. - Die Kettensäge ist cool, aber James muss nicht alle 5 Minuten eine ununterbrechbare und lange Animation machen, wie geil er sich mit dieser doch findet.  Ansonsten alles in allem 8/10 Meisterwerk, volle Empfehlung, selbst für Angsthasen

At first everything may feel confusing and unsettling, but every step you take reveal just a bit more of the truth behind the story.  Beneath all the terrifying atmosphere lies a surprisingly beautiful tragic love story. The game explores grief, guilt and love in a way that feels warm and heartfelt. By the time you reach the ending, everything clicks into place with an incredible reveal that can completely change the way the player views the journey.  What makes Silent Hill 2 unforgettable is how personal it feels. it makes you feel the weight of its story. It’s sad, it’s beautiful, and it stays with you long after the credits roll.

емейк-ремейк и ещё раз ремейк, ремейкали ремейк, фиксили Джеймса, а ненависть при ударах по врагам всё осталась.  Сюжет. Если вы играли в оригинал, то ничего нового не узнаете, разве что ваша игра 2001 года была немного растянута и вместо 5-6 часов, вы будете проходить ремейк порядка часов 13-14. Для взрослого ребёнка в виде меня, я доволен, пониманием игры, что я мастер 47 из 46 ачивок, что нет необходимости разжёвывать сюжет, будто я младенец или счастливый обладатель докторской степени в облизывание каждой детали по ярые приключения жорика. Сюжет даёт только ту часть которую нужно знать и не уходит слишком вглубь, вы изначально пришли в этот город ради Мэри и даже желая помочь другим посетителям данного города, вы всё равно продолжаете свои поиски, ведь у каждого есть свои демоны / тараканы и каждому нужно самому с ними справиться. Каждый видит город по-своему  Геймплей. Труба.... Бить врагов.... Доска с гвоздями.... бить врагов, моя рвать всех и пытаться не обделаться в процессе, уга буга оказаться сильнее, монке. Геймплей тривиален и если приноровится к атакам врага, то можно пройти всю игру с одной лишь трубой + доской, есть даже ачивка за это. От сего можно сделать вывод, что все необходимые ресурсы для прохождения игры, у вас есть с самого начала игры. Головоломки здесь интересные и хорошие, отдельно нравится что в игре есть настройки сложности головоломок, отчего повторные прохождения игры могут быть не менее интересными. Сложность боя отражается на геймплее стандартно, вы получаете больше урона, в то время как враги жирнее. .  Визуал + Саунд + Левел дизайн. Визуал, саунд, атмосфера всё это прямо таки на шикарном уровне, не сосчитать моментов сколько раз я сидел как вкопанный в стуле, просто от звука шёпота мне в ухо или потому что фоновый саунд заставлял меня думать, что сейчас придёт одна большая злая бабака и лишит меня всего моего достоинства. Уровни в свою очередь не являются чем-то сверхъестественным, но в целом это играет на плюс игре, ибо каждый из них уникален, как в плане его прохождения, так и самих загадок.   Игровой опыт в сельхоз культуру 2 можно описать как и любую сессионку. Playing Silent Hill 2 Remake on PC felt like stepping into a nightmare I didn’t want to wake from. The graphics are absolutely stunning—every foggy street and decaying hallway looks disturbingly real. I kept stopping just to take it all in, even when I knew something awful was lurking nearby.  Combat surprised me. It’s intense and nerve-wracking in the best way. Every encounter feels like a fight for survival, especially when ammo runs low and you’re forced to rely on whatever’s in reach. The sound design makes it even worse—in a good way. The ambient noise, the music, the way monsters groan and shuffle—it all got under my skin.  But what really stuck with me was the story. James’s journey is still one of the most haunting and emotionally raw narratives I’ve ever played. It doesn’t just scare you—it makes you think. I found myself reflecting on guilt, grief, and denial long after I shut the game off. That said, I’m really hoping they release the Born From A Wish DLC soon. Maria’s story adds so much depth, and without it, her character feels incomplete. I want to see her side of things—her pain, her motives.  All in all, this remake was incredible. It’s beautiful, terrifying, and deeply human.

I've long wanted to play the remake of one of my favorite games. However, it so happened that I only just finished the entire playthrough - and coincidentally, I'm writing this review on its first anniversary.  Firstly, I still can't believe this game was actually released. I bought it as a way of thanking Team Silent for giving the world such a unique series of games (which, among other things, influenced me). Secondly, I realized I’d be getting a remake of the second installment as well.  It's important to note that, simply due to the unavailability of both retro consoles and original game discs, it would have been difficult for the average player to experience the originals. Now, a new generation of players unfamiliar with the series can explore a modernized version in a convenient format.  I didn't have the chance to try the original game with its authentic gameplay experience. For enthusiasts like me, the Enhanced Edition was created, immersing me in the world of Silent Hill - and with that experience in mind, I constantly compared it to the remake. And you know what? Bloober Team managed to capture almost the entirety of that same atmosphere. During my first playthrough, I couldn’t believe I was reliving the same familiar story. You experience the same emotions as before - from the ambient soundscape of the quiet town (thanks again to the incomparable Akira Yamaoka for the soundtrack) to the oppressive atmosphere of the otherworldly realm.  And indeed, knowing every plot twist didn’t make the game boring at all. On the contrary, the developers almost completely redesigned the levels, making the familiar story feel fresh again. This makes it more engaging even for seasoned players who know the original by heart. The story itself hasn’t undergone any major changes - which is good for both newcomers who want to explore this project and returning fans who simply want to immerse themselves in the same world once more.  One downside is that the game runs on Unreal Engine 5. While I’ll admit the graphics look incredible, the visuals were so demanding that the gameplay suffered from constant frame-rate drops and general instability (which was actually one of the reasons why it took me so long to complete the game). For those with slower PCs, I recommend launching the game with the parameter “-dx11.” Naturally, this disables many of the engine’s advanced features, but it ensures a much more stable experience - at least, that’s what worked for me. The choice of engine is a topic for debate, but this review isn’t about that. The most important thing is that I was able to fully enjoy the game.  In conclusion, the Silent Hill 2 Remake is exactly what it should be. It preserves the spirit and atmosphere of the original while adapting the gameplay to a modern over-the-shoulder format. This gives players a new sense of freedom when controlling James, along with redesigned level architecture and new puzzles. If the reader is faced with the choice of playing the remake instead of the original, I can only encourage that decision - because the developers have meticulously preserved the soul of the game while adapting it to modern standards.  Thank you for reading. Peace to all.

El remake de Silent Hill 2 no solo revive uno de los títulos más icónicos de la historia del terror, sino que lo hace con una fidelidad y un cuidado que demuestran que todavía se puede respetar un clásico al tiempo que se lo actualiza para las audiencias de hoy. Desde el primer minuto, el regreso de James Sunderland a Silent Hill se siente como reencontrarse con una pesadilla conocida, pero con una fuerza renovada. La atmósfera es más opresiva que nunca gracias a un apartado técnico impecable: la niebla densa, las luces parciales, el sonido ambiental y cada crujido en la distancia logran una inmersión que incluso supera a la experiencia original.  La narrativa, piedra angular del juego, se mantiene intacta en su esencia, pero ahora está reforzada por animaciones faciales mucho más expresivas y un doblaje que transmite de forma desgarradora la vulnerabilidad de James. Ver cómo carga con su culpa y cómo se hunde poco a poco en la pesadilla es tan perturbador como lo fue en 2001, pero ahora con un realismo que golpea aún más fuerte. Las escenas clave —como el primer encuentro con Pyramid Head o el desarrollo de la relación con Maria— son escalofriantes, intensas y tratadas con una reverencia absoluta hacia el material original.  En lo jugable, el remake pule lo que antes podía sentirse tosco. El sistema de combate ahora es más fluido y responsivo, pero sin sacrificar la sensación de fragilidad que caracteriza a Silent Hill. James sigue siendo un hombre común atrapado en lo imposible, no un héroe de acción; cada enfrentamiento se siente tenso, peligroso, como debe ser. Los acertijos mantienen su esencia críptica y simbólica, evitando caer en la simplificación que a menudo arruina los remakes.  El apartado sonoro merece un párrafo aparte. Akira Yamaoka vuelve a brillar con una banda sonora que no solo reinterpreta los temas originales, sino que añade nuevas capas de melancolía y terror. La música, sumada al diseño sonoro (susurros, ecos, pasos en la niebla), convierte la exploración en una experiencia emocionalmente devastadora.  Lo más admirable es que el remake entiende perfectamente qué hizo grande al original: no eran solo los monstruos ni la ciudad embrujada, sino el retrato del dolor humano, la culpa y la desesperación. Silent Hill 2 siempre fue un viaje introspectivo disfrazado de survival horror, y esta nueva versión logra transmitirlo con la misma potencia, haciendo que jugadores veteranos revivan esa angustia y que los nuevos descubran por qué este título es considerado la obra maestra del género.  En definitiva, el remake de Silent Hill 2 es un triunfo rotundo: respeta el alma del clásico, actualiza lo necesario sin diluir la esencia y devuelve a Silent Hill al lugar que merece, como la cima del terror psicológico en los videojuegos. Es más que un simple remake; es una confirmación de que algunas pesadillas nunca mueren, solo regresan más nítidas, más intensas y más inolvidables.

I'll start off with that this game is my nr 1 favorite game oat. Just literally everything in this game is a piece of the puzzle that you're willing to solve the more you dive into the story. The old one had a great story but it didn't catch just as this remake. Every minute detail adds up to the pile of mysteries and sometimes even makes you believe you solved it all up until you get another detail. The second being James' mental state, his inner world, his mind and what actually is happening, every cutscene, note, every word and location detail sheds light on it. Absolute perfection of a game. Can't recommend it enough. From the story, to gameplay, to visuals, characters/monsters designs. And iconic Pyramid Head is a cherry on top. I could go on about this game forever, but I don't want to accidentally drop some spoiler or early explanation to what's going on. You just have to taste it on your own.

This is pure art. The entire game is steeped in symbolism and meaning down to every small detail. The characters are imperfect and flawed in very human ways, relatable and disgusting at the same time. The attention and care given to the narrative is a thing of beauty. I think it may very well be the best thing I've experienced.  The performance isn't great, but the graphics are eye catching. However, it was well worth the effort for the extra immersion. I highly recommend that route if you really want to get the most out of this game and have a high tolerance for horror.

I am an avid Silent Hill fan, I have played every Silent Hill game up until now.  This remake of the beloved PS2 Silent Hill 2 game is a perfect update to a beloved story in the franchise. The cinematics, character interactions, audio, graphics, and environment truly immerse the player in this horror masterpiece.  The only thing I didn't enjoy as much were the battles with enemies, especially without guns. Melee weapons are cumbersome to use and strafing type battling is very disorienting. Aside from this, everything else was perfect.  Puzzles were challenging, and the highlight of the game definitely was the exploration. Often you would come into a new level and check all the doors available to you, while clearing out enemies. The game did a good job alerting you to the locations of key items and puzzles or treasure chests.  The game is pretty dark overall, which adds to the sense of dread as vision in some underground or indoor settings is severely curtailed. The radio works to enhance the sense of anxiousness as it alerts you to incoming enemies as you explore.  The best part of the game definitely is towards the end, where the nightmare sections are vibrant, varied, and perfectly designed to fill you with nightmares. The boss battles also are difficult and epic.  The developers have done great justice to this game. I am very happy with the results.  It is highly recommended for all fans of horror games. Still do give the original PS2 game a play, it is a very different kind of game than this one.

Silent Hill 2 is one of the greatest games ever made, let alone one of the greatest Survival Horror games. It doesn't matter whether we are talking about the original or this remake. That still holds true.  The story of James Sunderland looking for his dead wife who he receives a letter from is just an incredible set up. The strange surreal nature of the character interactions, the incredible atmosphere provided by the town of Silent Hill, and the way the story unfolds were a deeply affecting experience that I will never forget. I am happy to report that this remake delivers even HARDER on the original vision of the game. It feels like exactly the game that they would have made with better technology and budget. The performances of every character are flawless without completely removing the awkward nature of the original.  You don't need me to tell you that the game is absolutely gorgeous. The town looks so real. It really feels like a place you could go to. The graphics look crisp and detailed up close and properly obscured by fog in the distance. All of the grotesque details of every environment are expertly crafted in the otherworld segments. Many moments of high resolution disgust to experience. The redesigns of the characters have been criticized by some, particularly Angela. They must have made some changes before release based on feedback because now she looks pretty much exactly the way she should. Meanwhile, Maria's redesign I think is perfect and does a much better job of portraying her character. The original soundtrack also makes a reappearance with some minor updates which are completely welcome. By the way, why the HELL does it not have a photo mode??  Another thing that has been updated from the original is the combat. I am sorry to tell you, all of the praise you have heard about the original game's combat is completely unwarranted. I say this as someone who loves that game, but being able to completely stun lock enemies as long as you keep attacking even on the harder difficulties is not really "gameplay." Now in this game you actually have to conserve ammo and use your melee weapon and switch between that and your guns on the fly. Dodging is also a thing and works well. Perfect for a survival horror game. Though the puzzles were great in the original, this game's puzzles are even better. They're hard to figure out and you feel pretty smart once you do.  All of this comes together as an incredible package. I understand to those who feel really deep nostalgia for the original game might be upset by some minor changes or feel that this game lacks some soul. I'm sorry, but I can't agree at all. This game is beautiful and respectful to the original and it has been improved in nearly every single way. Please play it!

Short version, Silent Hill 2's remake is one of the best games I've ever played and is a perfect entry spot for those uncomfortable with learning the old games' tank controls. It will make you feel dirty, sad and contemplative, as it should.  the long version...  Speaking as newly minted Silent Hill fan, going through the entire series (largely in release order), I can't speak fully either as a SH veteran with a long history nor as someone completely fresh to the franchise, being caught somewhere in the middle. That said, the original SH2 was frankly a disappointment the first time I played through it. Heralded as one of the greatest horror games and stories in video games, I knew I was alone in this. It wasn't its gameplay, atmosphere or pacing, mind you. The game's excellent and arguably the best of the first three judging by those elements alone. And that's coming from someone that adored first game and really liked 3 but 2... 2's story took awhile to warm on me as I just found OG James's insufferable.  Now, let's be clear. I'm really not one of those folks who hates sad and or weak main characters. My issue instead was that I found OG James creepy for most of my playthrough and I just couldn't sympathies with him. He felt like the archetypal (and I hate using this term) "nice guy", someone who's only nice because he feels like that's what's expected of him or to his benefit, but actually felt nothing towards others. Remake James meanwhile I wouldn't mind hanging out with. He'd be quiet and there would be "something" off about him, but I would just put it off as him going through a rough patch. Of course, things are complicated and there's more to both versions of James, but the differences being if I found out Remake James did something bad, I'd be shocked, while with OG James I'm just waiting to find out something. Many fans of the OG will argued that James is supposed to be off-putting as is the rest of the cast, but for me personally, it's a more effective atmosphere that I'm dreading the monsters and horrors, not encountering other people. There's still plenty off about the cast of SH2 Remake, but it's a lot more subtle, in large parts thanks to advanced motion capture and amazing performances, and I much prefer it. Gameplay wise, the remake is superb. I don't think anyone gonna deny that the remake is vast improvement in combat, which was pretty easy in the original outside of one or two annoying enemy types. Combat feels hefty and tense, making me calculate and weigh my options and resources when I spot enemies ahead or have to react in panic when I'm jumped. Boss battles are now actually boss fights, while the original killed whatever tension I might have had with everyone's favourite, pyramid head, in his long and annoying first boss fight where you just dodge his slow attacks for awhile in a small room.   Puzzles are mostly pretty good, with only the occasional headache that made me like I was going insane (I played on Hard puzzles for reference). The environments are absolutely top tier in industry, feeling large and allowing for those wonderful metroidvana brain clicks when areas loop back, but are simultaneously highly detailed and uncomfortably tight when fitting. The visuals teams deserves big credit for making Silent Hill's Otherworld tie a little more into other games versions of it whilst making it very distinctly its own between the wetness and overwhelming filth. Honest to god, part of me is disappointed James doesn't retain any grim and crap he gets covered in, but I'm also aware it would be have been tiring for him to look like 90% of the game without them adding a shower mechanic or something.  Some might be wondering how scary the game is, but I'm the wrong person to ask. I haven't found any third person games scary at this point in my life, with only SH3 getting to me in brief moments to its sound and creature designs hitting a personal nerve. That said, SH2 remake did make me jump the odd time (the mannequins can go to hell, thank you) and the grossness certainly made me uncomfortable, especially in those quick times event. Its sound design is also amazing and whomever made the choice to add those noises to the mannequins deserves a raise. So yeah, I won't call SH2 Remake scary, certainly uncomfortable and occasionally giving the odd surprise, but your mileage will vary if you're not desensitized to 90% of horror like I am.  Frankly, the only criticisms I can imagine someone having with this game are due to its interpretations of the story (which is highly subjective), its slower pace (fair, but the original had moments that were too fast, like meeting Angela then Eddie in the labyrinth), and if its combat is too powering or not enough (again, a highly subjective matter). That's rather incredible I feel for a game that could have gone so wrong and been rushed to make Konami a quick buck (*ahem* Downpour, Homecoming, etc), but Bloober Team absolutely delivered and for my money, made a great game even better. Absolutely amazing game, I can't believe I slept on this one for over 20 years. Highly recommended, especially if you enjoy survival horror.   The atmosphere in SH2 is perfect, from the dingy, run down small town streets to the oppressive corridors of abandoned apartments, the game is subtlety unsettling from start to finish. I am playing the game on standard combat difficulty and the survival horror elements are well done so far. You always feel just a little bit lower on resources than you'd like, without forcing you to die and reload your game a lot, which in my opinion would break the immersion.   Currently I am playing with the puzzle difficulty set to hard, and some of the puzzles so far have been real head scratchers, but solvable without a guide. Combat in this game is probably its weak link, as it's really nothing interesting or special. James is able to dodge and has a sprint, some enemies are easier to melee attack than others, sometimes it's better to run past enemies than engage them.   I have a fairly beefy gaming PC, so I'm able to play this game at max graphical settings with raytracing enabled with no issue. I experience no stuttering and with frame generation enabled, it's a very smooth experience with some occasional minor graphical artifacts caused by raytracing+frame gen.   Overall, the setting, pacing and story of this game are legendary, and so far Bloober Team has done an excellent job with SH2R.   Pros: - Amazing atmosphere - Great sound effects - Excellent moody soundtrack that sets the oppressive tone of the game - Excellent graphics - Interesting story - Rewarding exploration and puzzles  Cons: - Bland combat  - Minor graphical artifacting caused by raytracing + frame generation

Silent Hill 2 is simply one of the greatest horror games ever made. What makes it so special to me is how much of the fear comes from inside, not outside. The monsters, the fog, the town itself — everything feels like a reflection of James’s mind, his guilt, his grief, his need for punishment. It’s not just about being scared, it’s about being unsettled all the way down, and that’s what makes it unforgettable.  I love how everything in the game means something. Pyramid Head isn’t just a monster, he’s James’s guilt given form. The environments aren’t just creepy, they feel like memories rotting away. Even the other characters you meet feel like echoes of trauma, each carrying their own despair. It’s all so layered, and the more you think about it, the darker it gets.  The story is devastating. James isn’t some action hero — he’s broken, and as the truth unravels you realize just how tragic it all is. It’s rare for a game to make you feel horror and heartbreak at the same time, but Silent Hill 2 does it better than anything else I’ve played. The atmosphere, the pacing, the sound design, Akira Yamaoka’s music — every piece comes together perfectly.  It’s clunky sometimes, sure, especially the combat, but honestly I don’t even care. The awkwardness just makes the game feel heavier, slower, more suffocating. It’s part of the experience.  Silent Hill 2 isn’t just a horror game. It’s a masterpiece about grief, guilt, memory, and how far people will go to hide from or face the truth. It’s stuck with me more than any other horror game ever has, and probably always will.  Thanks Team Silent! :)

An outstanding game. A faithful yet innovative remake of the original 2001 title.   This game is haunting, melancholic, and thought-provoking. The themes were nailed perfectly here; it is a clear project of passion and appreciation for the original material. Every bit screams that it was hand-crafted intentionally, every detail well thought out and designed with purpose, both during gameplay, cutscenes, and even in menus. This remake features a surprisingly impressive range of accessibility customisation. I cannot state enough how massively appreciated Bloober Team's careful thought to implement every one of these options is. More on this later.  This game offers a special experience within the survival-horror genre due to its especially rich storytelling. I admire Silent Hill 2 for its thoughtful attention to detail, symbolism, and the way the environments tell the story more often than things being spoken outright. I devoured this game for the way it let me sink into it and become a part of the world, carefully dissecting each piece of it and pondering its meaning. Some things were surely more obvious than others, but I loved its constant invitation to *dig*.   Silent Hill 2 is stunning and immersive in both exploration and cinematics. Across the board, the vocal performances, animations, etc were completely spot-on decisions. If some award is not won for this, I'll honestly be shocked.  The combat isn't a particularly stand-out feature, lacking specialty and depth, but those aspects of the game are not intended to be the focus, and frankly never have been. Atmosphere and narrative have always been the focus of Silent Hill, and what makes the series so memorable and iconic to this very day. The original game was formatted in a way that required the player to control James from an almost birds-eye angle, the camera being fixed in one corner of the room. This lead to somewhat wonky controls, and makes for iconic yet frustrating gunplay in retrospect. Somewhat drawing from this, the Silent Hill 2 remake features equally "vanilla" gunplay, without bells and whistles that overcomplicate things without reason. The guns are slightly inaccurate seemingly regardless of how you attempt to handle them, but perhaps this was entirely intentional. Is James an experienced gun wielder, or is he just desperately attempting to fend off these walking nightmares?  I spent a big portion of the beginning of my play-through chuckling away as I charged about Silent Hill, smashing car windows and breaking into stores, as well as repeatedly stomping enemies' bodies after they'd jumps-cared me. This game was immense fun from start to finish, all while being perfectly disturbing, tense, and heartbreaking when it should have been.  But this enjoyment was not without some frustration.  I played on Medium settings, with certain features set to "off" where possible; a routine setup for my system regardless of the game.   Originally the iconic fog that has settled over Silent Hill didn't exist solely to create atmosphere, rather was a clever strategy to assist the original system - the PlayStation One -  in rendering nearby surroundings, and eliminate the need to focus on anything too far away. It was a smart benefit to the system at the time, yet now it's ironically a resource hog. The mist itself is not a solid block as it used to be, now causing frames to drop because of particle effects. I couldn't help but find this slightly comedic, given the original design purpose.   Despite my PC being well within (actually above) the recommended specifications, I try to eliminate as much as possible to allow for some breathing room whilst still maintaining visual quality. Unfortunately, despite my attempts to optimise the game, I suffered consistent frame-drops and stuttering from start to finish.   I was forced to lower the difficulty of combat because on many occasions I either died or wasted ammunition due to the performance issues. It did remove a layer of intensity on numerous occasions, as the briefly frozen frames provided a crack through the immersion so I could recover or react to whatever may have been going on at times.  Accessibility is something that I am deeply passionate about. I advocate for as much accessibility in gaming as possible wherever I can. I have made numerous complaints across different games regarding the inability to customise features to suit one's preferences or to assist one's disability. Games should be fun to experience, first and foremost. I wholeheartedly believe that everyone deserves a fair shot at something they aim to achieve if it's realistically within reach and they have the drive to do so.  Silent Hill 2 remake well and truly blew me away as one of the most inclusive and carefully considered games I've played personally. I cannot quite articulate how thrilled I was. It was truly something special to browse the menu and feel cared for, something myself and many others experience all to little of within gaming. Bloober Team's systems allowed customisation of a wide range of settings.   These included (but were not at all limited to):  HUD - Reticle Visibility (Off/Minimal/Dynamic - displays a range of reticle shapes and designs for various weapons) - Reticle Thickness (Thin/Normal/Thick - made the actual lines of the gun's reticle bolder and thus more apparent) - Reticle opacity (Slider - self-explanatory) - Low Health Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are coloured when James is injured) - Splatter Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are splattered when James is attacked)  INTERACTIONS - Interaction Icon Visibility (Off/Icon/Button Icon - choice of display type for interactable items, display just a dot or the button required to interact) - Interaction Icon Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - displays the previous setting much smaller or larger than default for easy spotting)  GRAPHICS - Colourblind Mode (Normal vision/Deuteranope/Protanope/Tritanope - self-explanatory) - Colourblind Mode Severity (Slider - changes vibrancy of colour-altered effects) - High Contrast Mode (Off/On - makes all scenery monochromatic grey, completely recolouring allies, enemies, environmental interactables, save points, and James himself for visibility. When "on", able to select White/Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Red/Green/Blue for each individual specified model.)  AUDIO  - Night Mode (Off/On - dampens the effect of typical loud sounds like "bang"s)  TEXTS  - Non-Verbal Captions Visibility (Off/On - things like *gate creaks*, and notable ambient sounds captioned) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size Font (Default/Bold/Dyslexic - self-explanatory.) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - self-explanatory) - Subtitle Names (Off/On - tells you who the speaker is in subtitled-text)  Each of these settings are located where you'd expect to find them depending on topic, however there is an additional screen entitled ACCESSIBILITY where it compiles all of these settings into one place for easy-access. It blew my mind that this game had so many options including a dedicated font for dyslexia. I nearly cried. I have OpenDyslexic font installed on my browser so that I can easily digest long strings of information when surfing the web. I never thought I'd actually see it implemented in a video-game.   I purchased the game from an external retailer, but on Steam, this title currently stands at $102.50 AUD. I'm uncertain if that's the same or much lower than what I paid upon release, but I believe it's reasonable for the overall fantastic experience this game provided.

Just finished this.   I gotta be honest with you, I think I was expecting more from a name as legendary in the gaming industry as Silent Hill 2.  Before playing, I was excited to finally be able to play Silent Hill 2 after hearing about it for literal decades. Frequently said to be the scariest game ever made, and the story regularly praised to the moon and back.  After playing, I was just kind of relieved that I was just over and done with the game. The game just feels far too bloated for how basic the gameplay is.  While I appreciated a lot of what the game has to offer, I did like the puzzles, the gameplay does feel draining after a while since there is literally only like 4 enemies in the game you'll be fighting against. See one of the basic enemies? Hit it with a pipe and dodge away before it blows up. Puppets? Beat the shit out of them with your pipe. Nurses? Beat the shit out of them with our pipe and occasionally gun them down if you don't feel like dealing with them. Repeat 15+ hours. The solution is every encounter is beating the shit out of everything with your pipe. It doesn't feel like an issue in the first half though, but you'll definitely feel the lack of gameplay variety as the game goes on. I was really feeling it by the time I reached the prison, and that's about 3/5 through the game. On top of that, Silent Hill 2 never really felt scary to me. I can name maybe 3 instances in the entire game where I was a little spooked. Tense and creepy? Yes. Scary? Rarely. Silent Hill 2 is probably a little bit scarier than RE4 Remake, less scary than Dead Space Remake. But that's coming from a major fan of Resident Evil 7, RE8's House Beneviento section, Outlast and Alien Isolation, so of course my expectations were gonna be high when it comes to scare factor.   Don't get me wrong, Silent Hill 2 has a lot of cool moments. The first half is excellent. Extremely dreadful, extremely tense, always masterfully pulling you along and asking yourself what is going to happen next, and how James's story is going to be slowly unravelled. The environments are incredibly detailed, atmosphere is harrowing as hell, the process of figuring out puzzles is really fun, music is haunting (but occasionally cheesy), exploration and level design is fun, boss fights are fun (except maybe the last two boss fights). Unfortunately, most of the game's narrative feels like an illogical carrot on a string. It unravels itself, yes, but it doesn't ever really give you a satisfying climax in the way I was expecting. It just stays in this wierd, vague, mysterious, ambiguous, nightmarish limbo that the rest of the story was submerged in. Always teasing you with something more, and barely delivering, letting the human mind fill the gaps. But I guess that's just the draw for Silent Hill. Everything is illogical. Even the enemy designs are that way. Things in Silent Hill are rarely explained, and when something IS explained, it's generally extremely vague, just enough to give you an idea of what is going on in this twisted and foggy town. Personally, I prefer something a little more blunt, storytelling wise.  I will say that I commend Luke Roberts's voice acting performance. He did a fantastic job. I will also say that Bloober Team has made a pretty good game here, against all odds. Before, Bloober has made incredibly mediocre games, so of course people were expecting this game to be mediocre as well. Bloober proved the doubters wrong. Silent Hill 2 Remake proves that Bloober has the talent to make something genuinely good.  I enjoyed this game, (I LOOOOVED this one section with Angela in particular) I just hope that Bloober continually improves themselves and learns from their experience with this game so we can get something truly incredible from them in the future, I think it'll be a while before that happens though.  8/10

De plus ce n'est pas un remaster mais bien un remake. Je vais donc en parler comme si l'original ne comptait pas.  Premièrement, techniquement, c'est à chié. Woah le futur de l'iréél engine 5, le machin est pas foutu de garder un framerate correcte quand tu te balade dans un couloir. C'est bourré de traversal stutters, et d'autre stutters en tout genre. Soit-disant les chargements c'est has-been mais charger des props/textures ou je ne sais quoi en plein combat c'est ridicule. Alors oui c'est beau, mais mon dieu j'ai rarement vu un jeu si cher aussi mal optimisé. Le pauvre stagiaire qui a bourré cette partie là et c'est toujours pas corrigé..........  Deuxièmement, le gameplay des combats... nuuul... j'ai l'impression de revenir sur un vieux jeu de PS1, lent, limité, et la maniabilité d'un tank bourré... bon OK, l'original est sur PS2, mais ils auraient pu faire un effort sur le gameplay.  La difficulté change un seul paramètre : la barre de vie des ennemis qui se transforme en sac à PV. OK, bon point, on peut rendre les ennemis nul en mode facile ce qui est pas trop mal et rajoute à l'ambiance.  Pour ce qui est du reste, c'est-à-dire de le vivre comme un walking simulator, avec une histoire, et quelques ennemis qui rajoute à l'ambiance. Wow, quelle claque. la D.A. incroyable, l'ambiance, tortueuse, labyrinthique, l'histoire qui a un vrai sens, dans lequel on ressent des choses avec les personnages. Franchement, du grand art. Sans les problèmes un peu chiant du dessus ça aurait été un 10/10 pour moi.  Sacré expérience à vivre, peut-être la seul chose à dire c'est que c'est vraiment *putain* de violent et infernal. Serrez votre ceinture.

[h1] Пример отличного ремейка. [/h1] По правде говоря, я - не проходил оригинальные части тихих холмов, и как по мне Silent Hill 2 remake от Bloober Team - лучший вариант для тех, кто не знаком с серией и хочет в нее вкатиться. Я прошел игру почти 2 раза и хотел бы поделиться своими впечатлениями о ней.  [h1] Сюжет [/h1] История повествует нам о Джеймсе Сандерленде, мужчине, который получил письмо от своей покойной жены Мэри и приезжает в Сайлент Хилл - город, с которым связано множество воспоминаний о его супруге. Может быть это чья-то шутка? А может... Мэри и в правду жива и ждет его? Больше про сюжет сказать не могу. Считаю, что с ним должен ознакомиться каждый лично.  [h1] Атмосфера [/h1] Начиная со стартовой сцены и вплоть до финала игра завораживает своей атмосферой. Густой туман, окутавший весь город, играющий не на шутку с воображением, как и звуки, доносящиеся из него. Быть может в нем что-то есть? Или же это просто воображение...  [h1] Графика [/h1] Касаемо графики хочется сказать так: это самая красивая игра по моему мнению на данный момент. Как по мне это тот случай, когда картинка в игре близка к фотореализму и за это хочется похвалить блуберов, они проделали отличную работу над визуалом.  [h1] Художественная составляющая [/h1] Арт-дизайн в игре - шикарный, разработчикам удалось отлично передать атмосферу и визуал заброшенного города, ржавого металла, раздолбанного асфальта, пустых улиц и прочего.  [h1] Музыка [/h1] Музыка в игре - шикарная. Идеально передает тон игры. Акира Ямаока как всегда - гений!  [h1] Геймплей [/h1] Геймплей в игре довольно интересный. Здесь присутствуют интересные головоломки, которые довольно приятные и радуют своей креативностью и подходом к решению. Правда есть одна проблема: перевод некоторых головоломок не особо корректный и не всегда понимаешь, как найти правильное решение. Поэтому людям, знающим английский язык - советую их проходить именно на нем, так будет проще. Боевая система в игре нормальная. Естественно она и близко не стоит рядом с серией Resident Evil, но, скажем так, боевка - сносная. Звуки огнестрела приятные, вроде бы даже прослеживается какой-то импакт от выстрелов и ударов холодным оружием.  [h1] Общие впечатления [/h1] А так, в целом, ничего больше добавить не могу. Хорошая, но печальная история о людях, любви, психологических травмах и последствиях принятых решений. Я испытал море положительных эмоций от прохождения данной игры и по праву считаю ее одним из лучших представителей жанра хорроров. Игра не раз пугала меня и держала в напряжении. Очень советую, просто попробуйте! Эта серия однозначно заслуживает вашего внимания!  Сюжет: 10/10 Графика: 10/10 Атмосфера: 10/10 Геймплей: 7-8/10 Музыка: 10/10

What can I say? I have never played a Silent Hill game. One of my friends has always told me its a great game, so I decided to try it out. Wishing I would have never even heard it was on PC because I could have saved myself 70 dollars. Sadly I purchased the game from G2A so I cant even ask for a refund from Steam. My fault for avoiding paying full price I guess... but worked out in the end because I would have been furious if I paid 100 dollars for this game. Where to begin....Performance. Frame rate is not an issue for me. I have absolutely no issue running this game MAX graphics with RT on with a stable 60 FPS. Its the absolutely absurd traversal micro stutter that is the issue here. It does not matter if my graphics are set to ALL LOW, it stutters in the same exact spots, every time. Even if you run through the whole level and try to properly build the shader cache. 80% OF THE GAME YOU CANT SEE 30 FEET IN FRONT OF YOU, BUT IM LAGGING WHILE RUNNING? Explain to me how I can run any game, High graphics, DLSS quality at 2k with 100+ fps with ZERO ISSUES, but I cant run this game on the lowest settings. THE ONLY work around for me is using NVIDIA rec. settings from the NVIDIA App (which is essentially medium settings), turn shadows to low (from suggestions via online research) then running 1080p with DLSS on performance. It doesnt look terrible, but its absolutely unacceptable. When I can play RDR2 with no issues, or Forza Horizon 5, Spider Man Remastered (also a notoriously bad PC port) and any other new game without any issues, something is wrong here. Alas, here we are in 2025. The game still hasn't been optimized properly, and they have released another game entirely without even fixing the broken one. They suggest to run the game at 30fps to avoid the stuttering.....guess what? you can literally still see the slow downs at 30 FPS. I have tried mods, fixes, DLSS swapper, capping frame rate to 30,40,50,60,75 and 90. Nothing works, the community gaslights you into believing the game isn't poorly optimized and that for some reason half the world cant build a PC properly. Ok. Bye, Felicia. Ich Persönlich kann für Silent 2 Hill keine Empfehlung geben zum Kaufen.  Folgende Gründe:  -Der Hauptgrund ist die Steuerung ( Controller ), sehr träge ( auch zuschauer im Stream haben das angemerkt.... sehr sehr schwach). Auch nachdem erhöhen der Werte für ein schnelles Drehen der Kamera in Y und X- Achse war das äußerst  schwach und träge. Noch mehr zum Tragen kam dieser Effekt wenn man im Zielmodus mit einer Waffe ist. In ca. 25 std. Spielzeit hat sich bis zum Ende kein Vertrautes Gefühl mit dem Umgang der Waffen eingestellt. Der Umgang mit Nahkampfwaffen ist weitesgehend ok, man kann sich Verteidigen. Aber auch hier gibt es negative Ereignisse,  Kämpft man gegen mehr als 2 gegen und einer wird zu Boden gebracht, und steht sehr dicht bei diesem und schlägt weiter zu nimmt er den zu Boden gebrachte (längst außer Gefecht) im Fokus und schlägt dann diesen weiter. Die Führung der Kamera in solchen fällen ist auch sehr schwach, sie Verfolgt den Schlag mit der Nahkampfwaffe bis in den Boden, in den Charakter selbst, zur Decke. Wände, oder Egoansicht mit Blick in einem Gegner usw. Immerwieder war man Zeitweise Blind.  Am meisten Tritt dieser Effekt leider in Schmalen Gängen, Fluren auf.  Ein nächster Punkt wäre die Grafik: Die Reale Welt fand ich gut, sie hat mit ein Gewisses Unwohlsein, Schaurigkeit bereitet. Top Die Alternative Welt hat es nur EINMAL geschafft diese Gefühle zu Verstärken, ansonsten Total  Schwache Immersion für mich. Die Gesichter der Charaktere im Game sind sehr ausdruckslos...... habe von einem Spiel aus Ende 2024 grafisch deutlich mehr erwartet.

“In my restless dreams, I see that town…” And every time I walk its foggy streets again, Silent Hill breaks me and heals me all at once.  This remake is unreal. An emotional rollercoaster, visually stunning, with an atmosphere that crawls under your skin and stays there. The places aren’t just locations — they’re distorted memories. Every hallway in the hospital, every fog-soaked alley, every room in that cursed hotel tells a story, even when no one’s speaking.  The characters aren’t just NPCs, they’re fragments of trauma thrown in your face with cruel elegance. James, Mary, Angela... each one hits like a punch to the heart.  And the music? Heart-wrenching. Quiet. Haunting. Akira Yamaoka’s soundtrack doesn’t just follow the story — it deepens it. Sometimes you just stand still in a room, letting it wash over you.  This isn’t just horror, it’s therapy in the shape of a nightmare. It pulls you in and doesn’t let go. And no matter how many times you play it, you always find a new way to suffer... and to fall in love with it all over again.  You don’t play a game like this. You live it. And then it stays with you.

Esqueça a palavra "remake". O que a Bloober Team fez com Silent Hill 2 transcende essa definição na minha humilde opinião. Esta não é só uma recriação, mas também uma complementação, uma expansão artística que pega uma das maiores obras-primas do terror e a eleva a um novo patamar de imersão e profundidade. É, sem a menor sombra de dúvida, cinema absoluto. O maior mérito desta nova versão é, para mim, sua coragem de reinterpretar. A repaginação das cenas clássicas é simplesmente magnífica, oferecendo uma nova ótica sobre momentos que pensávamos conhecer. A nova direção e a performance dos atores trazem uma força e uma nuance que aprofundam ainda mais a tragédia de James, Angela e todos os que vagam pela cidade da névoa. É como se fosse o mesmo poema, mas recitado de uma maneira nova, com outra emoção. No entanto, é importante ressaltar que esta obra ainda é e, provavelmente, sempre será Silent Hill 2. A atmosfera opressiva, o terror psicológico, os simbolismos, está tudo aqui, intacto e potencializado. Inclusive, a composição geral do jogo é incrível onde gráficos, design de som e jogabilidade modernizada trabalham em perfeita harmonia para servir à visão original. No meu panteão pessoal da franquia Silent Hill, este jogo não substitui o clássico. Ele se senta ao lado dele, dividindo o trono. Se você é fã da franquia ou do gênero de terror, terror psicológico, esta é uma jornada obrigatória e inesquecível.  NOTA: 10,0/10,0 ->ABSOLUTE CINEMA

I did not bother with turning on raytracing, not that I wanted it (would be nice with some darker levels) but because frame pacing is bad enough even without it. There is too much combat in this remake, with a combat system that is deliberately clumsy since James is a depressed dude. Problems come up with hit tracking. Many times he will just whiff or swings will pass through monsters.  Overall, this game is a must play for anyone with any interest in the godfather of psychological horror games. Does it suck? No. Does it blow the original out of the water? Also no. SH2 offers a solid modernized take the revolutionary classic.   I think it found a way to implement the "modern third-person shooter" mechanics and keeping them tight and functional, without taking away from making James feel like a normal dude on mission rather than a Special Forces officer. Graphically, the look of the town has never looked better. I liked the new scenes. There's only few enough that it adds flavor without feeling tacked on, and aside the them, the original dialogue 99% intact. The bosses are definitely a lot more intense if you played on hard difficulty. Puzzles are a lot easier, even on Hard, so make of that what you will.  My main gripes are mild ones, mostly with some of the sound design. Some of the musical cues don't match up at all with the original, and some of the voice acting left a bit to be desired. It's not like how SH2 2001 had awkward reads that gave it Lynch-esque surreality, just flatness that can take you out of the experience sometimes.  Had a lot of fun, though. Will definitely 100% and look forward to the SH1 remake.

Ganz ehrlich ich wollte einfach nur das es vorbei ist, das einzige was an ein Remake rankommt war der Prolog und das Hotel, die dann aber auch wirklich gut waren und Spaß gemacht haben, der Rest war wirklich nicht gut. Es ist okay für ein Remake ein neues Kampfsystem einzuführen, aber dann mach es richtig oder gar nicht, aber nicht diese kacke. Warum brauchte man zwingend einen Dodge? Hätte man den Dodge eingebaut und dann sowas wie eine Heavy und Light Attack eingebaut hätte könnte es vlt angenehm sein, aber man hat leider nur Schlagen oder nicht Schlagen und im Remake sind praktisch alle Gegner encounter Pflicht, man hat, nicht wie im Original, keine Möglichkeiten denen auszuweichen. Die Gegner folgen dir durch Türen, haben sehr unvorhersehbare Geschwindigkeiten, da sie für einen Angriff auch gerne zum Spieler teleportieren und Tauchen manchmal aus dem nichts auf, ohne dass das Radio ausschlägt, was das Weglaufen sehr erschwert.  Was das Level Design angeht, wurde bis auf das Hotel, die Stadt bis zur Bar und Teile vom Hospital das Game krass Liniar gemacht, war das Erkunden sehr langweilig und ermüdend gemacht hat. Manche Sachen wurden auch komplett umgeschrieben und ergeben keinen Sinn, wie z.B. das Reparieren der Schallplatte, wozu würde James, der nach seiner Frau sucht sich denken: "Oh ja die werd ich jetzt reparieren und mein Leben dafür riskieren die teile zu suchen"? Es ist einfach unnötig um Spielzeit zu strecken.  Zu dem allem kommt noch das die Kernessenz von der Silent Hill Reihe, die Rätsel, komplett verkackt wurden. Man sieht jetzt an einer durchsichtigen Umrandung, welche Gegenstände man braucht und wo man sie platzieren soll. Und Sachen wie z.B. das Uhrenrätsel keine Gehirnaktivität benötigt, weil man jetzt einfach Raten kann und es so sogar schneller geht. Und andere wie z.B. das Rätsel mit den Gewichten, wo es ganz klar andere Möglichkeiten gibt um die Gewichte richtig zu verteilen, das spiel aber nur eine Möglichkeit als richtig anerkennt.  All in all, eine komplette shitshow, ich würde empfehlen, das Spiel auf leichter Kampfschwierigkeit und schwerer Rätselschwierigkeit zu spielen oder, die weitaus bessere Wahl, es einfach gar nicht erst zu kaufen und sich lieber das Original auf einem Emulator zu spielen.
