емейк-ремейк и ещё раз ремейк, ремейкали ремейк, фиксили Джеймса, а ненависть при ударах по врагам всё осталась.  Сюжет. Если вы играли в оригинал, то ничего нового не узнаете, разве что ваша игра 2001 года была немного растянута и вместо 5-6 часов, вы будете проходить ремейк порядка часов 13-14. Для взрослого ребёнка в виде меня, я доволен, пониманием игры, что я мастер 47 из 46 ачивок, что нет необходимости разжёвывать сюжет, будто я младенец или счастливый обладатель докторской степени в облизывание каждой детали по ярые приключения жорика. Сюжет даёт только ту часть которую нужно знать и не уходит слишком вглубь, вы изначально пришли в этот город ради Мэри и даже желая помочь другим посетителям данного города, вы всё равно продолжаете свои поиски, ведь у каждого есть свои демоны / тараканы и каждому нужно самому с ними справиться. Каждый видит город по-своему  Геймплей. Труба.... Бить врагов.... Доска с гвоздями.... бить врагов, моя рвать всех и пытаться не обделаться в процессе, уга буга оказаться сильнее, монке. Геймплей тривиален и если приноровится к атакам врага, то можно пройти всю игру с одной лишь трубой + доской, есть даже ачивка за это. От сего можно сделать вывод, что все необходимые ресурсы для прохождения игры, у вас есть с самого начала игры. Головоломки здесь интересные и хорошие, отдельно нравится что в игре есть настройки сложности головоломок, отчего повторные прохождения игры могут быть не менее интересными. Сложность боя отражается на геймплее стандартно, вы получаете больше урона, в то время как враги жирнее. .  Визуал + Саунд + Левел дизайн. Визуал, саунд, атмосфера всё это прямо таки на шикарном уровне, не сосчитать моментов сколько раз я сидел как вкопанный в стуле, просто от звука шёпота мне в ухо или потому что фоновый саунд заставлял меня думать, что сейчас придёт одна большая злая бабака и лишит меня всего моего достоинства. Playing Silent Hill 2 Remake on PC felt like stepping into a nightmare I didn’t want to wake from. The graphics are absolutely stunning—every foggy street and decaying hallway looks disturbingly real. I kept stopping just to take it all in, even when I knew something awful was lurking nearby.  Combat surprised me. It’s intense and nerve-wracking in the best way. Every encounter feels like a fight for survival, especially when ammo runs low and you’re forced to rely on whatever’s in reach. The sound design makes it even worse—in a good way. The ambient noise, the music, the way monsters groan and shuffle—it all got under my skin.  But what really stuck with me was the story. James’s journey is still one of the most haunting and emotionally raw narratives I’ve ever played. It doesn’t just scare you—it makes you think. I found myself reflecting on guilt, grief, and denial long after I shut the game off. That said, I’m really hoping they release the Born From A Wish DLC soon. Maria’s story adds so much depth, and without it, her character feels incomplete. I want to see her side of things—her pain, her motives.  All in all, this remake was incredible. It’s beautiful, terrifying, and deeply human.

I've long wanted to play the remake of one of my favorite games. However, it so happened that I only just finished the entire playthrough - and coincidentally, I'm writing this review on its first anniversary.  Firstly, I still can't believe this game was actually released. I bought it as a way of thanking Team Silent for giving the world such a unique series of games (which, among other things, influenced me). Secondly, I realized I’d be getting a remake of the second installment as well.  It's important to note that, simply due to the unavailability of both retro consoles and original game discs, it would have been difficult for the average player to experience the originals. Now, a new generation of players unfamiliar with the series can explore a modernized version in a convenient format.  I didn't have the chance to try the original game with its authentic gameplay experience. For enthusiasts like me, the Enhanced Edition was created, immersing me in the world of Silent Hill - and with that experience in mind, I constantly compared it to the remake. And you know what? Bloober Team managed to capture almost the entirety of that same atmosphere. During my first playthrough, I couldn’t believe I was reliving the same familiar story. You experience the same emotions as before - from the ambient soundscape of the quiet town (thanks again to the incomparable Akira Yamaoka for the soundtrack) to the oppressive atmosphere of the otherworldly realm.  And indeed, knowing every plot twist didn’t make the game boring at all. On the contrary, the developers almost completely redesigned the levels, making the familiar story feel fresh again. This makes it more engaging even for seasoned players who know the original by heart. The story itself hasn’t undergone any major changes - which is good for both newcomers who want to explore this project and returning fans who simply want to immerse themselves in the same world once more.  One downside is that the game runs on Unreal Engine 5. While I’ll admit the graphics look incredible, the visuals were so demanding that the gameplay suffered from constant frame-rate drops and general instability (which was actually one of the reasons why it took me so long to complete the game). For those with slower PCs, I recommend launching the game with the parameter “-dx11.” Naturally, this disables many of the engine’s advanced features, but it ensures a much more stable experience - at least, that’s what worked for me. The choice of engine is a topic for debate, but this review isn’t about that. The most important thing is that I was able to fully enjoy the game.  In conclusion, the Silent Hill 2 Remake is exactly what it should be. It preserves the spirit and atmosphere of the original while adapting the gameplay to a modern over-the-shoulder format. This gives players a new sense of freedom when controlling James, along with redesigned level architecture and new puzzles. If the reader is faced with the choice of playing the remake instead of the original, I can only encourage that decision - because the developers have meticulously preserved the soul of the game while adapting it to modern standards.  Thank you for reading. Peace to all.

this game is REALLY good, but... THE PERFORMANCE. I cannot stress enough how terribly this game runs. I have a good computer- maybe not quite "good" by today's standards, but it can run similar games like Resident Evil 4, 7 and 2, the Dead Space remake, and Amnesia: The Bunker just fine. What the genuine hell is the excuse for this game suddenly dropping to like, fifteen frames a second? Would it have killed them to add some loading screens? Would it have hurt to provide any good options for lowering the visual quality for the sake of performance- because that's what really irks me. I'm fine with my game not really looking the best it could. I'd love for it to look the best it can, but we don't always get what we want, do we? It becomes a genuine problem for me, though, when in the middle of fighting an enemy or even BOSS, my frames tank and i can barely even play the game. I don't even know what causes some of the frame drops. Loading new areas, of course, but randomly the framerate just kicks the bucket and I don't know why. It's something that I dealt with- I never had too many issues BECAUSE of the framerate but GOD it was annoying and genuinely hurt the experience for me. This is unacceptable- a SEVENTY DOLLAR SURVIVAL HORROR GAME that can't even reach 60 FPS unless you're staring directly at a corner. How did the game ship like this? Better yet- how has the game gone an entire YEAR without them adding adequate graphics and optimization settings, or fixing the source of the issue? Again, this is unacceptable. Visually this game isn't even like, stunning or anything. It's just realistic and it has good art direction, which doesn't necessitate a billion polygons and rays of light or whatever the hell even causes the abysmal framerate anyway.  Outside of the performance, Silent Hill 2 is a PHENOMENAL game. The combat is engaging, fun and tense, the atmosphere is top-notch, overall the game is just absolutely horrific, and everybody already knows that the story of Silent Hill 2 is one of the all-time greats. It's a great game, I just really wish it didn't have to have such lousy performance.

Antes de jugar este remake, decidí jugar primero los Silent Hill y Silent Hill 2 originales. Quería entender las diferencias y comprobar si se conservaba la visión de los creadores. Y aunque no se trata de un remake 1:1, considero que mejora de manera excepcional al juego original; todo lo que añade le suma de forma increíble a la experiencia.  El diseño de niveles es fantástico, el combate ha sido mejorado sin perder la esencia original, y los nuevos puzzles están mucho más trabajados. Además, la jugabilidad y la cámara (algo que era de esperar) pues se sienten mucho más fluidas, y la música es sencillamente increíble.  En cuanto a la historia, el juego original ya era extraordinario, pero este remake introduce pequeñas variaciones que tienen mucho más sentido dentro del conjunto narrativo. Aun así, mantiene intacta la esencia que lo convierte en una auténtica obra de arte.  En síntesis, Silent Hill 2 - Remake es una obra maestra actualizada a tiempos modernos que vale mucho la pena jugar.  100% recomendado!

El remake de Silent Hill 2 no solo revive uno de los títulos más icónicos de la historia del terror, sino que lo hace con una fidelidad y un cuidado que demuestran que todavía se puede respetar un clásico al tiempo que se lo actualiza para las audiencias de hoy. Desde el primer minuto, el regreso de James Sunderland a Silent Hill se siente como reencontrarse con una pesadilla conocida, pero con una fuerza renovada. La atmósfera es más opresiva que nunca gracias a un apartado técnico impecable: la niebla densa, las luces parciales, el sonido ambiental y cada crujido en la distancia logran una inmersión que incluso supera a la experiencia original.  La narrativa, piedra angular del juego, se mantiene intacta en su esencia, pero ahora está reforzada por animaciones faciales mucho más expresivas y un doblaje que transmite de forma desgarradora la vulnerabilidad de James. Ver cómo carga con su culpa y cómo se hunde poco a poco en la pesadilla es tan perturbador como lo fue en 2001, pero ahora con un realismo que golpea aún más fuerte. Las escenas clave —como el primer encuentro con Pyramid Head o el desarrollo de la relación con Maria— son escalofriantes, intensas y tratadas con una reverencia absoluta hacia el material original.  En lo jugable, el remake pule lo que antes podía sentirse tosco. El sistema de combate ahora es más fluido y responsivo, pero sin sacrificar la sensación de fragilidad que caracteriza a Silent Hill. James sigue siendo un hombre común atrapado en lo imposible, no un héroe de acción; cada enfrentamiento se siente tenso, peligroso, como debe ser. Los acertijos mantienen su esencia críptica y simbólica, evitando caer en la simplificación que a menudo arruina los remakes.  El apartado sonoro merece un párrafo aparte. Akira Yamaoka vuelve a brillar con una banda sonora que no solo reinterpreta los temas originales, sino que añade nuevas capas de melancolía y terror. La música, sumada al diseño sonoro (susurros, ecos, pasos en la niebla), convierte la exploración en una experiencia emocionalmente devastadora.  Lo más admirable es que el remake entiende perfectamente qué hizo grande al original: no eran solo los monstruos ni la ciudad embrujada, sino el retrato del dolor humano, la culpa y la desesperación. Silent Hill 2 siempre fue un viaje introspectivo disfrazado de survival horror, y esta nueva versión logra transmitirlo con la misma potencia, haciendo que jugadores veteranos revivan esa angustia y que los nuevos descubran por qué este título es considerado la obra maestra del género.  En definitiva, el remake de Silent Hill 2 es un triunfo rotundo: respeta el alma del clásico, actualiza lo necesario sin diluir la esencia y devuelve a Silent Hill al lugar que merece, como la cima del terror psicológico en los videojuegos. Es más que un simple remake; es una confirmación de que algunas pesadillas nunca mueren, solo regresan más nítidas, más intensas y más inolvidables.

I'll start off with that this game is my nr 1 favorite game oat. Just literally everything in this game is a piece of the puzzle that you're willing to solve the more you dive into the story. The second being James' mental state, his inner world, his mind and what actually is happening, every cutscene, note, every word and location detail sheds light on it. Absolute perfection of a game. I am an avid Silent Hill fan, I have played every Silent Hill game up until now.  This remake of the beloved PS2 Silent Hill 2 game is a perfect update to a beloved story in the franchise. The cinematics, character interactions, audio, graphics, and environment truly immerse the player in this horror masterpiece.  The only thing I didn't enjoy as much were the battles with enemies, especially without guns. Melee weapons are cumbersome to use and strafing type battling is very disorienting. Aside from this, everything else was perfect.  Puzzles were challenging, and the highlight of the game definitely was the exploration. Often you would come into a new level and check all the doors available to you, while clearing out enemies. The game did a good job alerting you to the locations of key items and puzzles or treasure chests.  The game is pretty dark overall, which adds to the sense of dread as vision in some underground or indoor settings is severely curtailed. The radio works to enhance the sense of anxiousness as it alerts you to incoming enemies as you explore.  The best part of the game definitely is towards the end, where the nightmare sections are vibrant, varied, and perfectly designed to fill you with nightmares. The boss battles also are difficult and epic.  The developers have done great justice to this game. I am very happy with the results.  It is highly recommended for all fans of horror games. Still do give the original PS2 game a play, it is a very different kind of game than this one.

Silent Hill 2 is one of the greatest games ever made, let alone one of the greatest Survival Horror games. It doesn't matter whether we are talking about the original or this remake. That still holds true.  The story of James Sunderland looking for his dead wife who he receives a letter from is just an incredible set up. The strange surreal nature of the character interactions, the incredible atmosphere provided by the town of Silent Hill, and the way the story unfolds were a deeply affecting experience that I will never forget. I am happy to report that this remake delivers even HARDER on the original vision of the game. It feels like exactly the game that they would have made with better technology and budget. The performances of every character are flawless without completely removing the awkward nature of the original.  You don't need me to tell you that the game is absolutely gorgeous. The town looks so real. It really feels like a place you could go to. The graphics look crisp and detailed up close and properly obscured by fog in the distance. All of the grotesque details of every environment are expertly crafted in the otherworld segments. Many moments of high resolution disgust to experience. The redesigns of the characters have been criticized by some, particularly Angela. They must have made some changes before release based on feedback because now she looks pretty much exactly the way she should. Meanwhile, Maria's redesign I think is perfect and does a much better job of portraying her character. The original soundtrack also makes a reappearance with some minor updates which are completely welcome. By the way, why the HELL does it not have a photo mode??  Another thing that has been updated from the original is the combat. I am sorry to tell you, all of the praise you have heard about the original game's combat is completely unwarranted. I say this as someone who loves that game, but being able to completely stun lock enemies as long as you keep attacking even on the harder difficulties is not really "gameplay." Now in this game you actually have to conserve ammo and use your melee weapon and switch between that and your guns on the fly. Dodging is also a thing and works well. Perfect for a survival horror game. Though the puzzles were great in the original, this game's puzzles are even better. They're hard to figure out and you feel pretty smart once you do.  All of this comes together as an incredible package. I understand to those who feel really deep nostalgia for the original game might be upset by some minor changes or feel that this game lacks some soul. I'm sorry, but I can't agree at all. This game is beautiful and respectful to the original and it has been improved in nearly every single way. Please play it!

Speaking as newly minted Silent Hill fan, going through the entire series (largely in release order), I can't speak fully either as a SH veteran with a long history nor as someone completely fresh to the franchise, being caught somewhere in the middle. That said, the original SH2 was frankly a disappointment the first time I played through it. Heralded as one of the greatest horror games and stories in video games, I knew I was alone in this. It wasn't its gameplay, atmosphere or pacing, mind you. The game's excellent and arguably the best of the first three judging by those elements alone. And that's coming from someone that adored first game and really liked 3 but 2... 2's story took awhile to warm on me as I just found OG James's insufferable.  Now, let's be clear. I'm really not one of those folks who hates sad and or weak main characters. My issue instead was that I found OG James creepy for most of my playthrough and I just couldn't sympathies with him. He felt like the archetypal (and I hate using this term) "nice guy", someone who's only nice because he feels like that's what's expected of him or to his benefit, but actually felt nothing towards others. Remake James meanwhile I wouldn't mind hanging out with. He'd be quiet and there would be "something" off about him, but I would just put it off as him going through a rough patch. Of course, things are complicated and there's more to both versions of James, but the differences being if I found out Remake James did something bad, I'd be shocked, while with OG James I'm just waiting to find out something. Many fans of the OG will argued that James is supposed to be off-putting as is the rest of the cast, but for me personally, it's a more effective atmosphere that I'm dreading the monsters and horrors, not encountering other people. There's still plenty off about the cast of SH2 Remake, but it's a lot more subtle, in large parts thanks to advanced motion capture and amazing performances, and I much prefer it. Gameplay wise, the remake is superb. I don't think anyone gonna deny that the remake is vast improvement in combat, which was pretty easy in the original outside of one or two annoying enemy types. Combat feels hefty and tense, making me calculate and weigh my options and resources when I spot enemies ahead or have to react in panic when I'm jumped. Boss battles are now actually boss fights, while the original killed whatever tension I might have had with everyone's favourite, pyramid head, in his long and annoying first boss fight where you just dodge his slow attacks for awhile in a small room.   Puzzles are mostly pretty good, with only the occasional headache that made me like I was going insane (I played on Hard puzzles for reference). The environments are absolutely top tier in industry, feeling large and allowing for those wonderful metroidvana brain clicks when areas loop back, but are simultaneously highly detailed and uncomfortably tight when fitting. The visuals teams deserves big credit for making Silent Hill's Otherworld tie a little more into other games versions of it whilst making it very distinctly its own between the wetness and overwhelming filth. Honest to god, part of me is disappointed James doesn't retain any grim and crap he gets covered in, but I'm also aware it would be have been tiring for him to look like 90% of the game without them adding a shower mechanic or something.  Some might be wondering how scary the game is, but I'm the wrong person to ask. I haven't found any third person games scary at this point in my life, with only SH3 getting to me in brief moments to its sound and creature designs hitting a personal nerve. That said, SH2 remake did make me jump the odd time (the mannequins can go to hell, thank you) and the grossness certainly made me uncomfortable, especially in those quick times event. Its sound design is also amazing and whomever made the choice to add those noises to the mannequins deserves a raise. So yeah, I won't call SH2 Remake scary, certainly uncomfortable and occasionally giving the odd surprise, but your mileage will vary if you're not desensitized to 90% of horror like I am.  Frankly, the only criticisms I can imagine someone having with this game are due to its interpretations of the story (which is highly subjective), its slower pace (fair, but the original had moments that were too fast, like meeting Angela then Eddie in the labyrinth), and if its combat is too powering or not enough (again, a highly subjective matter). That's rather incredible I feel for a game that could have gone so wrong and been rushed to make Konami a quick buck (*ahem* Downpour, Homecoming, etc), but Bloober Team absolutely delivered and for my money, made a great game even better.  I excited yet terrified for their upcoming Silent Hill 1 remake.

Silent Hill 2 is simply one of the greatest horror games ever made. What makes it so special to me is how much of the fear comes from inside, not outside. The monsters, the fog, the town itself — everything feels like a reflection of James’s mind, his guilt, his grief, his need for punishment. It’s not just about being scared, it’s about being unsettled all the way down, and that’s what makes it unforgettable.  I love how everything in the game means something. Pyramid Head isn’t just a monster, he’s James’s guilt given form. The environments aren’t just creepy, they feel like memories rotting away. Even the other characters you meet feel like echoes of trauma, each carrying their own despair. It’s all so layered, and the more you think about it, the darker it gets.  The story is devastating. James isn’t some action hero — he’s broken, and as the truth unravels you realize just how tragic it all is. It’s rare for a game to make you feel horror and heartbreak at the same time, but Silent Hill 2 does it better than anything else I’ve played. The atmosphere, the pacing, the sound design, Akira Yamaoka’s music — every piece comes together perfectly.  It’s clunky sometimes, sure, especially the combat, but honestly I don’t even care. The awkwardness just makes the game feel heavier, slower, more suffocating. It’s part of the experience.  Silent Hill 2 isn’t just a horror game. It’s a masterpiece about grief, guilt, memory, and how far people will go to hide from or face the truth. It’s stuck with me more than any other horror game ever has, and probably always will.  Thanks Team Silent! :)

An outstanding game. A faithful yet innovative remake of the original 2001 title.   This game is haunting, melancholic, and thought-provoking. The themes were nailed perfectly here; it is a clear project of passion and appreciation for the original material. Every bit screams that it was hand-crafted intentionally, every detail well thought out and designed with purpose, both during gameplay, cutscenes, and even in menus. This remake features a surprisingly impressive range of accessibility customisation. I cannot state enough how massively appreciated Bloober Team's careful thought to implement every one of these options is. More on this later.  This game offers a special experience within the survival-horror genre due to its especially rich storytelling. I admire Silent Hill 2 for its thoughtful attention to detail, symbolism, and the way the environments tell the story more often than things being spoken outright. I devoured this game for the way it let me sink into it and become a part of the world, carefully dissecting each piece of it and pondering its meaning. Some things were surely more obvious than others, but I loved its constant invitation to *dig*.   Silent Hill 2 is stunning and immersive in both exploration and cinematics. Across the board, the vocal performances, animations, etc were completely spot-on decisions. If some award is not won for this, I'll honestly be shocked.  The combat isn't a particularly stand-out feature, lacking specialty and depth, but those aspects of the game are not intended to be the focus, and frankly never have been. Atmosphere and narrative have always been the focus of Silent Hill, and what makes the series so memorable and iconic to this very day. The original game was formatted in a way that required the player to control James from an almost birds-eye angle, the camera being fixed in one corner of the room. This lead to somewhat wonky controls, and makes for iconic yet frustrating gunplay in retrospect. Somewhat drawing from this, the Silent Hill 2 remake features equally "vanilla" gunplay, without bells and whistles that overcomplicate things without reason. The guns are slightly inaccurate seemingly regardless of how you attempt to handle them, but perhaps this was entirely intentional. Is James an experienced gun wielder, or is he just desperately attempting to fend off these walking nightmares?  I spent a big portion of the beginning of my play-through chuckling away as I charged about Silent Hill, smashing car windows and breaking into stores, as well as repeatedly stomping enemies' bodies after they'd jumps-cared me. This game was immense fun from start to finish, all while being perfectly disturbing, tense, and heartbreaking when it should have been.  But this enjoyment was not without some frustration.  I played on Medium settings, with certain features set to "off" where possible; a routine setup for my system regardless of the game.   Originally the iconic fog that has settled over Silent Hill didn't exist solely to create atmosphere, rather was a clever strategy to assist the original system - the PlayStation One -  in rendering nearby surroundings, and eliminate the need to focus on anything too far away. It was a smart benefit to the system at the time, yet now it's ironically a resource hog. The mist itself is not a solid block as it used to be, now causing frames to drop because of particle effects. I couldn't help but find this slightly comedic, given the original design purpose.   Despite my PC being well within (actually above) the recommended specifications, I try to eliminate as much as possible to allow for some breathing room whilst still maintaining visual quality. Unfortunately, despite my attempts to optimise the game, I suffered consistent frame-drops and stuttering from start to finish.   I was forced to lower the difficulty of combat because on many occasions I either died or wasted ammunition due to the performance issues. It did remove a layer of intensity on numerous occasions, as the briefly frozen frames provided a crack through the immersion so I could recover or react to whatever may have been going on at times.  Accessibility is something that I am deeply passionate about. I advocate for as much accessibility in gaming as possible wherever I can. I have made numerous complaints across different games regarding the inability to customise features to suit one's preferences or to assist one's disability. Games should be fun to experience, first and foremost. I wholeheartedly believe that everyone deserves a fair shot at something they aim to achieve if it's realistically within reach and they have the drive to do so.  Silent Hill 2 remake well and truly blew me away as one of the most inclusive and carefully considered games I've played personally. I cannot quite articulate how thrilled I was. It was truly something special to browse the menu and feel cared for, something myself and many others experience all to little of within gaming. Bloober Team's systems allowed customisation of a wide range of settings.   These included (but were not at all limited to):  HUD - Reticle Visibility (Off/Minimal/Dynamic - displays a range of reticle shapes and designs for various weapons) - Reticle Thickness (Thin/Normal/Thick - made the actual lines of the gun's reticle bolder and thus more apparent) - Reticle opacity (Slider - self-explanatory) - Low Health Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are coloured when James is injured) - Splatter Vignette (off/on - choose whether the borders of the screen are splattered when James is attacked)  INTERACTIONS - Interaction Icon Visibility (Off/Icon/Button Icon - choice of display type for interactable items, display just a dot or the button required to interact) - Interaction Icon Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - displays the previous setting much smaller or larger than default for easy spotting)  GRAPHICS - Colourblind Mode (Normal vision/Deuteranope/Protanope/Tritanope - self-explanatory) - Colourblind Mode Severity (Slider - changes vibrancy of colour-altered effects) - High Contrast Mode (Off/On - makes all scenery monochromatic grey, completely recolouring allies, enemies, environmental interactables, save points, and James himself for visibility. When "on", able to select White/Cyan/Magenta/Yellow/Red/Green/Blue for each individual specified model.)  AUDIO  - Night Mode (Off/On - dampens the effect of typical loud sounds like "bang"s)  TEXTS  - Non-Verbal Captions Visibility (Off/On - things like *gate creaks*, and notable ambient sounds captioned) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size Font (Default/Bold/Dyslexic - self-explanatory.) - Subtitle/Tips/Tutorials/Transcription Size (Tiny/Small/Medium/Big/Huge - self-explanatory) - Subtitle Names (Off/On - tells you who the speaker is in subtitled-text)  Each of these settings are located where you'd expect to find them depending on topic, however there is an additional screen entitled ACCESSIBILITY where it compiles all of these settings into one place for easy-access. It blew my mind that this game had so many options including a dedicated font for dyslexia. I nearly cried. I have OpenDyslexic font installed on my browser so that I can easily digest long strings of information when surfing the web. I never thought I'd actually see it implemented in a video-game.   I purchased the game from an external retailer, but on Steam, this title currently stands at $102.50 AUD. I'm uncertain if that's the same or much lower than what I paid upon release, but I believe it's reasonable for the overall fantastic experience this game provided.

A fully fleshed out game (pun intended). It can be hard to justify $70, but this game was truly an extended, immersive experience.   Pros: -The level of detail and the graphics are INSANE. The characters are much more realistic. (when i heard it was "woke" i knew it was gonna be good). From pictures/screenshots it may seem like the characters look odd, but when you're actually in the game & interacting with them: its much more realistic, emotive, detailed, and it all makes sense. It gives "Monster House" for adults vibes. -New endings -New puzzles -It honored not only the original Silent Hill 2 game- but also the original and all of the games by Team Silent. -More immersion into the world -The combat is MUCH smoother -This game fills in a lot of the gaps in the original SH2. You still have to infer things, and its still FILLED with metaphors: but everything is more fully fleshed out. I do think it aligns with what the original idea that Team Silent had, back when they made it. But back in the day: PS2 games were rarely this long. So you had to draw a lot of conclusions yourself, or look up theories. I like that this was a fully-told, hauntingly-beautiful, story. -There is no such thing as "Easy" mode. There is a "Light" mode, which is still extremely challenging & difficult to do. I dont know if this is a pro, or a con, but I know a lot of gamers like to be challenged: so im including it with the pros.  Cons: -There is a bug during the Xray puzzle: where the x-rays that were initially on the wall: disappear when you come back, after collecting the missing x-ray. To fix this: go save your game, reload it, and all of the photos should be there when you load it up again. -Some items just cannot be picked up. This didnt affect gameplay or success though. -Some small visual bugs like guns not physically appearing in hands, but you can still shoot them -The voices were really hard to hear over the sound effects. I wish there was a way to turn that up, without having explosive audio shortly afterwards. -Some of the puzzles, even on light mode: are nearly impossible without a guide. There are just no hints at all for some of the puzzles, and you basically just have to figure it out. So you would be there for many hours. -Silent Hill loves a good prison segment, honey. And of course the prison portion of this game is the most maddening & the worst.

Just finished this.   I gotta be honest with you, I think I was expecting more from a name as legendary in the gaming industry as Silent Hill 2.  Before playing, I was excited to finally be able to play Silent Hill 2 after hearing about it for literal decades. Frequently said to be the scariest game ever made, and the story regularly praised to the moon and back.  After playing, I was just kind of relieved that I was just over and done with the game. The game just feels far too bloated for how basic the gameplay is.  While I appreciated a lot of what the game has to offer, I did like the puzzles, the gameplay does feel draining after a while since there is literally only like 4 enemies in the game you'll be fighting against. See one of the basic enemies? Hit it with a pipe and dodge away before it blows up. Puppets? Beat the shit out of them with your pipe. Nurses? Beat the shit out of them with our pipe and occasionally gun them down if you don't feel like dealing with them. Repeat 15+ hours. The solution is every encounter is beating the shit out of everything with your pipe. It doesn't feel like an issue in the first half though, but you'll definitely feel the lack of gameplay variety as the game goes on. I was really feeling it by the time I reached the prison, and that's about 3/5 through the game. On top of that, Silent Hill 2 never really felt scary to me. I can name maybe 3 instances in the entire game where I was a little spooked. Tense and creepy? Yes. Scary? Rarely. Silent Hill 2 is probably a little bit scarier than RE4 Remake, less scary than Dead Space Remake. But that's coming from a major fan of Resident Evil 7, RE8's House Beneviento section, Outlast and Alien Isolation, so of course my expectations were gonna be high when it comes to scare factor.   Don't get me wrong, Silent Hill 2 has a lot of cool moments. The first half is excellent. Extremely dreadful, extremely tense, always masterfully pulling you along and asking yourself what is going to happen next, and how James's story is going to be slowly unravelled. The environments are incredibly detailed, atmosphere is harrowing as hell, the process of figuring out puzzles is really fun, music is haunting (but occasionally cheesy), exploration and level design is fun, boss fights are fun (except maybe the last two boss fights). Unfortunately, most of the game's narrative feels like an illogical carrot on a string. It unravels itself, yes, but it doesn't ever really give you a satisfying climax in the way I was expecting. It just stays in this wierd, vague, mysterious, ambiguous, nightmarish limbo that the rest of the story was submerged in. Always teasing you with something more, and barely delivering, letting the human mind fill the gaps. But I guess that's just the draw for Silent Hill. Everything is illogical. Even the enemy designs are that way. Things in Silent Hill are rarely explained, and when something IS explained, it's generally extremely vague, just enough to give you an idea of what is going on in this twisted and foggy town. Personally, I prefer something a little more blunt, storytelling wise.  I will say that I commend Luke Roberts's voice acting performance. He did a fantastic job. I will also say that Bloober Team has made a pretty good game here, against all odds. Before, Bloober has made incredibly mediocre games, so of course people were expecting this game to be mediocre as well. Bloober proved the doubters wrong. Silent Hill 2 Remake proves that Bloober has the talent to make something genuinely good.  I enjoyed this game, (I LOOOOVED this one section with Angela in particular) I just hope that Bloober continually improves themselves and learns from their experience with this game so we can get something truly incredible from them in the future, I think it'll be a while before that happens though.  8/10

De plus ce n'est pas un remaster mais bien un remake. Je vais donc en parler comme si l'original ne comptait pas.  Premièrement, techniquement, c'est à chié. Woah le futur de l'iréél engine 5, le machin est pas foutu de garder un framerate correcte quand tu te balade dans un couloir. C'est bourré de traversal stutters, et d'autre stutters en tout genre. Soit-disant les chargements c'est has-been mais charger des props/textures ou je ne sais quoi en plein combat c'est ridicule. Alors oui c'est beau, mais mon dieu j'ai rarement vu un jeu si cher aussi mal optimisé. Le pauvre stagiaire qui a bourré cette partie là et c'est toujours pas corrigé..........  Deuxièmement, le gameplay des combats... nuuul... j'ai l'impression de revenir sur un vieux jeu de PS1, lent, limité, et la maniabilité d'un tank bourré... bon OK, l'original est sur PS2, mais ils auraient pu faire un effort sur le gameplay.  La difficulté change un seul paramètre : la barre de vie des ennemis qui se transforme en sac à PV. OK, bon point, on peut rendre les ennemis nul en mode facile ce qui est pas trop mal et rajoute à l'ambiance.  Pour ce qui est du reste, c'est-à-dire de le vivre comme un walking simulator, avec une histoire, et quelques ennemis qui rajoute à l'ambiance. Wow, quelle claque. la D.A. incroyable, l'ambiance, tortueuse, labyrinthique, l'histoire qui a un vrai sens, dans lequel on ressent des choses avec les personnages. Franchement, du grand art. Sans les problèmes un peu chiant du dessus ça aurait été un 10/10 pour moi.  Sacré expérience à vivre, peut-être la seul chose à dire c'est que c'est vraiment *putain* de violent et infernal. 📝 English review below / Reseña en inglés más abajo  ⸻  🔶 El terror más profundo no viene de afuera, viene de adentro.  ⸻  📝 RESEÑA EN ESPAÑOL  Voy a contar un poco mi historia con este juego. La primera vez que lo jugué fue en la década de los 2000, cuando todavía no llegaba a los 15 años. No logré pasar ni un tercio porque me daba demasiado miedo, así que terminé abandonándolo.  Hoy, muchos años después, me doy cuenta de algo más fuerte: no solo no lo iba a terminar, sino que tampoco lo iba a entender. Este Silent Hill no se limita a dar miedo con monstruos o escenarios oscuros, sino que toca el verdadero terror: el que genera nuestra propia mente. Habla de traumas, de culpas, de rencores… y nos muestra que la batalla más grande es contra nosotros mismos.  Como decía Carl Jung con el concepto de la sombra, este juego nos enfrenta con esa parte oscura de nuestra psique que escondemos por miedo. En ese sentido, Silent Hill 2 Remake es tan realista como perturbador: no se trata solo de sobrevivir, sino de mirarnos en un espejo incómodo.  Lo recomiendo a quienes estén preparados para algo más que un survival horror. Porque puede ayudarnos a ser más sinceros con nosotros mismos y, en consecuencia, también con los demás.  ⸻  ✅ Puntos positivos: • Una historia profunda y psicológica. • Terror que trasciende lo superficial. • Personajes y atmósfera que dejan huella. • Excelente reinterpretación en el remake.  ❌ Puntos negativos: • No es para cualquiera: puede ser demasiado perturbador. • Jugabilidad que en algunos momentos se siente pesada. • Exige estar en el “estado mental” correcto para apreciarlo.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusión:  Más que un juego de terror, es un viaje a lo más oscuro de la mente humana. Silent Hill 2 Remake no solo asusta: confronta, incomoda y deja pensando. Una experiencia única para quienes se animen a mirarse dentro.  🔸 PUNTUACIÓN FINAL: 9/10 El miedo más real es el que llevamos dentro.  ⸻  📝 REVIEW IN ENGLISH  🔶 The deepest fear doesn’t come from the outside — it comes from within.  ⸻  Let me share a bit of my story with this game. The first time I played it was back in the 2000s, when I was under 15 years old. I couldn’t get past even a third of the game because it scared me so much, so I abandoned it.  Today, looking back as an adult, I realize something bigger: not only was I not going to finish it, I wasn’t even going to understand it. This Silent Hill doesn’t just scare with monsters or dark environments — it dives into the fear created by our own minds. It’s about trauma, guilt, resentment… and it shows us that the greatest battle is against ourselves.  As Carl Jung described with the concept of the shadow, this game confronts us with the darkest part of our psyche that we hide out of fear. In that sense, Silent Hill 2 Remake is as realistic as it is disturbing: it’s not just about surviving, it’s about facing an uncomfortable reflection.  I recommend it to those who are ready for something deeper than a survival horror. It can genuinely help us treat ourselves — and others — more sincerely.  ⸻  ✅ Pros: • Deep, psychological storytelling. • Fear that goes beyond the superficial. • Memorable characters and atmosphere. • Strong reinterpretation in the remake.  ❌ Cons: • Not for everyone: can be too disturbing. • Gameplay can feel heavy at times. • Requires the right mental state to fully appreciate.  ⸻  🎯 Conclusion:  More than a horror game, it’s a journey into the darkest corners of the human mind. Silent Hill 2 Remake doesn’t just scare — it confronts, unsettles, and lingers. A unique experience for those brave enough to look within.  🔸 FINAL SCORE: 9/10 The scariest fear is the one we carry inside.

[h1] Пример отличного ремейка. [/h1] По правде говоря, я - не проходил оригинальные части тихих холмов, и как по мне Silent Hill 2 remake от Bloober Team - лучший вариант для тех, кто не знаком с серией и хочет в нее вкатиться. Я прошел игру почти 2 раза и хотел бы поделиться своими впечатлениями о ней.  [h1] Сюжет [/h1] История повествует нам о Джеймсе Сандерленде, мужчине, который получил письмо от своей покойной жены Мэри и приезжает в Сайлент Хилл - город, с которым связано множество воспоминаний о его супруге. Может быть это чья-то шутка? А может... Мэри и в правду жива и ждет его? Больше про сюжет сказать не могу. Считаю, что с ним должен ознакомиться каждый лично.  [h1] Атмосфера [/h1] Начиная со стартовой сцены и вплоть до финала игра завораживает своей атмосферой. Густой туман, окутавший весь город, играющий не на шутку с воображением, как и звуки, доносящиеся из него. Быть может в нем что-то есть? Или же это просто воображение...  [h1] Графика [/h1] Касаемо графики хочется сказать так: это самая красивая игра по моему мнению на данный момент. Как по мне это тот случай, когда картинка в игре близка к фотореализму и за это хочется похвалить блуберов, они проделали отличную работу над визуалом.  [h1] Художественная составляющая [/h1] Арт-дизайн в игре - шикарный, разработчикам удалось отлично передать атмосферу и визуал заброшенного города, ржавого металла, раздолбанного асфальта, пустых улиц и прочего.  [h1] Музыка [/h1] Музыка в игре - шикарная. Идеально передает тон игры. Акира Ямаока как всегда - гений!  [h1] Геймплей [/h1] Геймплей в игре довольно интересный. Здесь присутствуют интересные головоломки, которые довольно приятные и радуют своей креативностью и подходом к решению. Правда есть одна проблема: перевод некоторых головоломок не особо корректный и не всегда понимаешь, как найти правильное решение. Поэтому людям, знающим английский язык - советую их проходить именно на нем, так будет проще. Боевая система в игре нормальная. Естественно она и близко не стоит рядом с серией Resident Evil, но, скажем так, боевка - сносная. Звуки огнестрела приятные, вроде бы даже прослеживается какой-то импакт от выстрелов и ударов холодным оружием.  [h1] Общие впечатления [/h1] А так, в целом, ничего больше добавить не могу. Хорошая, но печальная история о людях, любви, психологических травмах и последствиях принятых решений. Я испытал море положительных эмоций от прохождения данной игры и по праву считаю ее одним из лучших представителей жанра хорроров. Игра не раз пугала меня и держала в напряжении. Очень советую, просто попробуйте! Эта серия однозначно заслуживает вашего внимания!  Сюжет: 10/10 Графика: 10/10 Атмосфера: 10/10 Геймплей: 7-8/10 Музыка: 10/10

What can I say? I have never played a Silent Hill game. One of my friends has always told me its a great game, so I decided to try it out. Wishing I would have never even heard it was on PC because I could have saved myself 70 dollars. Sadly I purchased the game from G2A so I cant even ask for a refund from Steam. My fault for avoiding paying full price I guess... but worked out in the end because I would have been furious if I paid 100 dollars for this game. Where to begin....Performance. Frame rate is not an issue for me. I have absolutely no issue running this game MAX graphics with RT on with a stable 60 FPS. Its the absolutely absurd traversal micro stutter that is the issue here. It does not matter if my graphics are set to ALL LOW, it stutters in the same exact spots, every time. Even if you run through the whole level and try to properly build the shader cache. 80% OF THE GAME YOU CANT SEE 30 FEET IN FRONT OF YOU, BUT IM LAGGING WHILE RUNNING? Explain to me how I can run any game, High graphics, DLSS quality at 2k with 100+ fps with ZERO ISSUES, but I cant run this game on the lowest settings. THE ONLY work around for me is using NVIDIA rec. settings from the NVIDIA App (which is essentially medium settings), turn shadows to low (from suggestions via online research) then running 1080p with DLSS on performance. It doesnt look terrible, but its absolutely unacceptable. When I can play RDR2 with no issues, or Forza Horizon 5, Spider Man Remastered (also a notoriously bad PC port) and any other new game without any issues, something is wrong here. Alas, here we are in 2025. The game still hasn't been optimized properly, and they have released another game entirely without even fixing the broken one. They suggest to run the game at 30fps to avoid the stuttering.....guess what? you can literally still see the slow downs at 30 FPS. I have tried mods, fixes, DLSS swapper, capping frame rate to 30,40,50,60,75 and 90. Nothing works, the community gaslights you into believing the game isn't poorly optimized and that for some reason half the world cant build a PC properly. Ok. Bye, Felicia. Ich Persönlich kann für Silent 2 Hill keine Empfehlung geben zum Kaufen.  Folgende Gründe:  -Der Hauptgrund ist die Steuerung ( Controller ), sehr träge ( auch zuschauer im Stream haben das angemerkt.... sehr sehr schwach). Auch nachdem erhöhen der Werte für ein schnelles Drehen der Kamera in Y und X- Achse war das äußerst  schwach und träge. Noch mehr zum Tragen kam dieser Effekt wenn man im Zielmodus mit einer Waffe ist. In ca. 25 std. Spielzeit hat sich bis zum Ende kein Vertrautes Gefühl mit dem Umgang der Waffen eingestellt. Der Umgang mit Nahkampfwaffen ist weitesgehend ok, man kann sich Verteidigen. Aber auch hier gibt es negative Ereignisse,  Kämpft man gegen mehr als 2 gegen und einer wird zu Boden gebracht, und steht sehr dicht bei diesem und schlägt weiter zu nimmt er den zu Boden gebrachte (längst außer Gefecht) im Fokus und schlägt dann diesen weiter. Die Führung der Kamera in solchen fällen ist auch sehr schwach, sie Verfolgt den Schlag mit der Nahkampfwaffe bis in den Boden, in den Charakter selbst, zur Decke. Wände, oder Egoansicht mit Blick in einem Gegner usw. Immerwieder war man Zeitweise Blind.  Am meisten Tritt dieser Effekt leider in Schmalen Gängen, Fluren auf.  Ein nächster Punkt wäre die Grafik: Die Reale Welt fand ich gut, sie hat mit ein Gewisses Unwohlsein, Schaurigkeit bereitet. Top Die Alternative Welt hat es nur EINMAL geschafft diese Gefühle zu Verstärken, ansonsten Total  Schwache Immersion für mich. Die Gesichter der Charaktere im Game sind sehr ausdruckslos...... habe von einem Spiel aus Ende 2024 grafisch deutlich mehr erwartet.

嗯...女生建模有点丑，头身比例不太对。头太大了。第一次拿出时间想玩，玩了两个小时继续不下去了。第二次强迫自己，加上查攻略给通关了。通关后有种解脱的感觉。流程没必要做这么长，开头的流程可以设计的更抓人一点，有点无聊了。直到第一次进里世界开始有兴趣继续玩下去了。我觉得流程短一点，价格便宜一点会让这个游戏更出彩，玩到后边会很累，不一口气玩完会降低带入感。场景美术是极其出彩的，男主配音感觉也很有那种哀伤的感觉。设定很好，但是这个题材，詹姆斯自己这点事支持不住这么精彩的设计。三角头压迫感不够，不如电影版。血腥度感觉也差很多。我感觉这个游戏绝对没到完美的神作那个地步，可以优化的点很多。我没玩过老版，只看过电影版，我觉得电影版的三角头更有压迫感，电影版那个虫子也更好一些。怪种类也比较少。 总结，这个游戏不好玩，剧情也挺水，这点破事没必要整这么假深刻。游戏的优点是设定和场景设计。全流程玩下来有些折磨自己，但是通关后不会有浪费时间的心情，不算白玩。解密熟了以后通关后有开多周目的欲望。看的出来人家也没有为了追求好玩去做这个游戏。虽然有些折磨，但是推荐爱玩单机的要体验一下。恐怖游戏千篇一律很多，解密游戏也有很多类似。只能说这个游戏很独特。

“In my restless dreams, I see that town…” And every time I walk its foggy streets again, Silent Hill breaks me and heals me all at once.  This remake is unreal. An emotional rollercoaster, visually stunning, with an atmosphere that crawls under your skin and stays there. The places aren’t just locations — they’re distorted memories. Every hallway in the hospital, every fog-soaked alley, every room in that cursed hotel tells a story, even when no one’s speaking.  The characters aren’t just NPCs, they’re fragments of trauma thrown in your face with cruel elegance. James, Mary, Angela... each one hits like a punch to the heart.  And the music? Heart-wrenching. Quiet. Haunting. Akira Yamaoka’s soundtrack doesn’t just follow the story — it deepens it. Sometimes you just stand still in a room, letting it wash over you.  This isn’t just horror, it’s therapy in the shape of a nightmare. It pulls you in and doesn’t let go. And no matter how many times you play it, you always find a new way to suffer... and to fall in love with it all over again.  You don’t play a game like this. You live it. And then it stays with you.

Esqueça a palavra "remake". O que a Bloober Team fez com Silent Hill 2 transcende essa definição na minha humilde opinião. Esta não é só uma recriação, mas também uma complementação, uma expansão artística que pega uma das maiores obras-primas do terror e a eleva a um novo patamar de imersão e profundidade. É, sem a menor sombra de dúvida, cinema absoluto. O maior mérito desta nova versão é, para mim, sua coragem de reinterpretar. A repaginação das cenas clássicas é simplesmente magnífica, oferecendo uma nova ótica sobre momentos que pensávamos conhecer. A nova direção e a performance dos atores trazem uma força e uma nuance que aprofundam ainda mais a tragédia de James, Angela e todos os que vagam pela cidade da névoa. É como se fosse o mesmo poema, mas recitado de uma maneira nova, com outra emoção. No entanto, é importante ressaltar que esta obra ainda é e, provavelmente, sempre será Silent Hill 2. A atmosfera opressiva, o terror psicológico, os simbolismos, está tudo aqui, intacto e potencializado. Inclusive, a composição geral do jogo é incrível onde gráficos, design de som e jogabilidade modernizada trabalham em perfeita harmonia para servir à visão original. No meu panteão pessoal da franquia Silent Hill, este jogo não substitui o clássico. Ele se senta ao lado dele, dividindo o trono. Se você é fã da franquia ou do gênero de terror, terror psicológico, esta é uma jornada obrigatória e inesquecível.  NOTA: 10,0/10,0 ->ABSOLUTE CINEMA

Does it suck? No. Does it blow the original out of the water? Also no. SH2 offers a solid modernized take the revolutionary classic.   I think it found a way to implement the "modern third-person shooter" mechanics and keeping them tight and functional, without taking away from making James feel like a normal dude on mission rather than a Special Forces officer. Graphically, the look of the town has never looked better. I liked the new scenes. There's only few enough that it adds flavor without feeling tacked on, and aside the them, the original dialogue 99% intact. The bosses are definitely a lot more intense if you played on hard difficulty. Puzzles are a lot easier, even on Hard, so make of that what you will.  My main gripes are mild ones, mostly with some of the sound design. Some of the musical cues don't match up at all with the original, and some of the voice acting left a bit to be desired. It's not like how SH2 2001 had awkward reads that gave it Lynch-esque surreality, just flatness that can take you out of the experience sometimes.  Had a lot of fun, though. Will definitely 100% and look forward to the SH1 remake.

Ganz ehrlich ich wollte einfach nur das es vorbei ist, das einzige was an ein Remake rankommt war der Prolog und das Hotel, die dann aber auch wirklich gut waren und Spaß gemacht haben, der Rest war wirklich nicht gut. Es ist okay für ein Remake ein neues Kampfsystem einzuführen, aber dann mach es richtig oder gar nicht, aber nicht diese kacke. Warum brauchte man zwingend einen Dodge? Hätte man den Dodge eingebaut und dann sowas wie eine Heavy und Light Attack eingebaut hätte könnte es vlt angenehm sein, aber man hat leider nur Schlagen oder nicht Schlagen und im Remake sind praktisch alle Gegner encounter Pflicht, man hat, nicht wie im Original, keine Möglichkeiten denen auszuweichen. Die Gegner folgen dir durch Türen, haben sehr unvorhersehbare Geschwindigkeiten, da sie für einen Angriff auch gerne zum Spieler teleportieren und Tauchen manchmal aus dem nichts auf, ohne dass das Radio ausschlägt, was das Weglaufen sehr erschwert.  Was das Level Design angeht, wurde bis auf das Hotel, die Stadt bis zur Bar und Teile vom Hospital das Game krass Liniar gemacht, war das Erkunden sehr langweilig und ermüdend gemacht hat. Manche Sachen wurden auch komplett umgeschrieben und ergeben keinen Sinn, wie z.B. das Reparieren der Schallplatte, wozu würde James, der nach seiner Frau sucht sich denken: "Oh ja die werd ich jetzt reparieren und mein Leben dafür riskieren die teile zu suchen"? Es ist einfach unnötig um Spielzeit zu strecken.  Zu dem allem kommt noch das die Kernessenz von der Silent Hill Reihe, die Rätsel, komplett verkackt wurden. Man sieht jetzt an einer durchsichtigen Umrandung, welche Gegenstände man braucht und wo man sie platzieren soll. Und Sachen wie z.B. das Uhrenrätsel keine Gehirnaktivität benötigt, weil man jetzt einfach Raten kann und es so sogar schneller geht. Und andere wie z.B. das Rätsel mit den Gewichten, wo es ganz klar andere Möglichkeiten gibt um die Gewichte richtig zu verteilen, das spiel aber nur eine Möglichkeit als richtig anerkennt.  All in all, eine komplette shitshow, ich würde empfehlen, das Spiel auf leichter Kampfschwierigkeit und schwerer Rätselschwierigkeit zu spielen oder, die weitaus bessere Wahl, es einfach gar nicht erst zu kaufen und sich lieber das Original auf einem Emulator zu spielen.

Silent Hill 2 – Ein zeitloses Meisterwerk des psychologischen Horrors  Silent Hill 2 ist nicht einfach nur ein Spiel – es ist ein emotionaler Abgrund, ein kunstvolles Mosaik aus Schuld, Trauer und Wahnsinn.   Schon beim ersten Betreten der nebligen Stadt spürt man, dass Silent Hill 2 anders ist. Die beklemmende Stille, unterbrochen von bedrückenden Geräuschen und dem unvergesslichen Soundtrack von Akira Yamaoka, zieht einen sofort in den Bann. Der Einsatz von Musik und Stille ist meisterhaft – jede Note sitzt, jede Pause hat Bedeutung.  Die Story um James Sunderland, der einen Brief von seiner verstorbenen Frau erhält und sich auf die Suche nach ihr in der düsteren Stadt macht, ist tiefgründig, symbolisch und schockierend ehrlich. Was als klassischer Horror beginnt, entwickelt sich zu einer psychologischen Reise in die dunkelsten Ecken der menschlichen Seele. Jeder Charakter, dem man begegnet – von der tragischen Maria bis zum verstörenden Eddie – wirkt wie ein Spiegel von James’ innerem Zustand. Nichts ist oberflächlich, alles hat Bedeutung.  Was mich persönlich am meisten berührt hat: Ich konnte mich in diesem Spiel selbst wiederfinden. Die Fragen, die es stellt – über Schuld, Verlust, Verdrängung und inneren Schmerz – sind keine fiktiven Konzepte. Sie sind real. Silent Hill 2 ist kein Fantasy-Horror. Es ist ein Spiegel, der dir dein eigenes Inneres zeigt. Es hat mich dazu gebracht, über mich selbst nachzudenken – über Entscheidungen, über Emotionen, über das, was man manchmal lieber tief vergraben lässt. In gewisser Weise war es eine Reise zu mir selbst. Dieses Spiel hat mehr mit dem echten Leben zu tun, als man auf den ersten Blick glauben mag.  Die Stadt Silent Hill selbst ist mehr als nur ein Schauplatz – sie ist ein lebendiger Albtraum, der sich der Psyche des Spielers und der Hauptfigur anpasst. Die düstere Architektur, die sich verändernden Umgebungen, die grotesken Kreaturen – alles fügt sich nahtlos in das narrative Gesamtkunstwerk ein.  Fazit: Silent Hill 2 ist kein gewöhnliches Horrorspiel. Es ist Kunst. Es ist eine emotionale Reise, die sich tief ins Gedächtnis einbrennt. Von der unvergleichlichen Atmosphäre über den ikonischen Soundtrack bis zur meisterhaft geschriebenen Geschichte – dieses Spiel ist ein unsterbliches Meisterwerk. Und für mich persönlich war es sogar mehr: Es war ein Spiegel, ein Weckruf, ein Stück Selbsterkenntnis.

I want to start off this review by saying that I have never played the original Silent Hill 2. I don't know if this remake "holds-up" or is as good as the original. With that being said this is one of the greatest horror games ever made, and one of the greatest stories in general. The combat is fun but not too crazy, but at the same time you are kept on your toes. The puzzles are challenging but not too difficult that they become frustrating, and so it is really satisfying to solve them. The graphics are amazing, all the little details around the town, you can tell they really thought this out. The locations are iconic and memorable. The sound design is some of the best I've heard in a video game. Not because it is insanely innovative or anything, but I've never been so afraid in a game solely because of the noises I would hear. There's a part where you're in a dark tunnel and you hear what sounds like giant footsteps clambering towards you. I was in immense panic and kept running out of the tunnel, thinking something was chasing me. But, upon further inspection, it was some kind of creature under the grates on the floor crawling around. All this to say, is that the sound design produced stress, paranoia, and genuine fear into me while playing. The story is really well done. [spoiler] I already had known the big plot twist, but I still was surprised at certain parts and it still is a good game even if you have had it spoiled to you. [/spoiler] Please go into the game as blind as possible. The characters are all interesting as you learn more about them. I will say sometimes the facial animation in cutscenes can feel a little off, but it's not too bad. When you finish the game, you start to see all the symbolism the game uses. (I mean, I didn't understand what the heck was happening), and I highly recommend reading about it online or watching a video about it after playing the game. Silent Hill 2 is one of the best horror games, and video games in general. I wouldn't exactly recommend it at the price it's listed as of writing this review (70$), but if it's on sale definitely grab it. Even if you don't do well with horror games, you should still try it. It doesn't heavily rely on jumpscares, but rather it has building tension and fear through the unknown. Overall an excellent game and well worth your time.

This is a survival horror masterpiece, independent of your appreciation of the original. It has the best of everything that survival horror has to offer, and then some.   The combat is mechanically deep enough to incorporate strategy, and there is a fair bit of it. I like the new combat a lot, the enemies are fast and erratic and James is slow and unsteady. Enemies will scatter and hide in the dark, and ambush you with perfect timing. It's more grounded than games like Resident Evil 4 or Dead Space, but still more action heavy than the original silent hill. Despite the frequency of combat, I still found encounters to be tense and mannequins provided relentless jump scares. The bosses were overall great, and a large improvement to the originals as well.  The puzzles and exploration are what separates this from a lot of other modern, OTS camera style horror games. There are a lot of puzzles, and they are elaborate, multi-step processes that carry over into other rooms, that are usually locked by keys or puzzle sequences linked to other rooms. Nearly every section of the game is like a maze, nothing is ever a straight line and you can never tell what's ahead because it's either too dark, or too foggy.   You're constantly feeling lost while being hunted in the dark, scavenging through run down buildings filled with monsters and dark imagery. The sound design brings it all together, with haunting music and sounds that generally make me want to quit the game. Silent Hill's music has the worst vibes, a symphony of sirens, metal banging on metal, strange distortions, all designed to make you feel bad. It's a perfect horror soundtrack.  It's a pretty long game, 16-20 hours for a first run. Every mechanic gets used to its full potential, there is a lot of combat, a lot of puzzles, and a lot of ground to explore. It remains faithful to the original while providing an even more hardcore experience and more challenging level design. Technical issues aside, it's a must play.

How does someone wipe off their sins when the blood becomes stained, and the perception of your surroundings begin to weigh in? Horror games feel so brushed off in the gaming landscape considering now that most modern catalog of horror games are filled with cheap jumpscares and copy and pasted content. While there have been plenty of good horror games in the past few years, Silent Hill 2 is a reminder of what the standard of horror games should always strive to be. The atmosphere and the environment never makes it feel that you're in one place, one moment could be returning to reality and the next moment you'll be hearing the cries down the hospital hallway. The characters speak so weirdly and although it can be chalked up to be bad voice acting, the voices and out of place characters add so much to how it reflects James and what kind of person he is.   Silent Hill 2 is a must play, even for people who do not like horror games, I can only beg that you try out this masterpiece.

⭐ Silent Hill 2 Remake – O retorno que o inferno merecia!  Cara… que experiência. Eu entrei nesse remake com o pé atrás, achando que talvez mexer demais num clássico fosse estragar a magia. Mas olha, a Bloober Team conseguiu algo que eu sinceramente não esperava: eles respeitaram a essência do original e ainda conseguiram dar uma nova alma pra ele.  Logo de cara, o visual me deixou sem palavras. Cada sombra, cada partícula de neblina, cada reflexo na água, tudo parece respirar junto com a dor e o desespero do James. A cidade de Silent Hill nunca pareceu tão viva e ao mesmo tempo tão morta. E o som… MEU DEUS, o som. Joga de fone e me diz se não é de arrepiar cada passo que você dá naquele corredor escuro.  O combate está mais fluido, mais responsivo, e mesmo assim não perdeu aquele peso psicológico que te faz pensar se vale a pena lutar ou simplesmente fugir. Não virou um jogo de ação, continua sendo um terror de atmosfera, onde o medo vem muito mais do silêncio do que dos sustos.  Mas o que realmente me pegou foi o emocional. Mesmo já conhecendo a história, ver tudo isso reimaginado com atuações e expressões tão realistas mexeu comigo de novo. O remake consegue fazer você sentir empatia, desconforto e até um tipo estranho de melancolia. É um terror que fala sobre culpa, amor e perda, e isso é o que faz Silent Hill 2 ser o que é.  Sou psicólogo, e esse lado da trama sempre me chamou atenção. Silent Hill 2 é praticamente uma metáfora sobre o inconsciente, onde cada criatura, cada cenário e até o silêncio refletem o estado mental do James. O remake captura perfeitamente essa dor interna, esse conflito entre culpa e redenção. É um jogo que fala sobre o luto, o autoengano e a necessidade de encarar o que escondemos de nós mesmos. Wyobraź sobie sytuację, że po ciężkiej, tajemniczej chorobie umiera bliska Ci osoba. Czujesz ból, rozpacz po jej stracie, a po przeżyciu żałoby próbujesz wrócić na prostą. Aż nagle dostajesz list, który okazuje się być napisany przez tę osobę. Pisze w nim, że chciałaby się z Tobą spotkać w miejscu, które znaliście i lubiliście. „To jakiś pokręcony żart”, myślisz w duchu, ale jakaś drzemiąca w Tobie cząstka uznaje, że trzeba to sprawdzić. Tak zazwyczaj zaczynają się wyjątkowo tragiczne w skutkach historie, prawda?  Bohaterem owej historii jest James, który to po pewnym czasie od straty ukochanej żony otrzymał napisany przez nią list, w którym wyznaje, że czeka na niego w Silent Hill, które za jej życia było ich „specjalnym miejscem”. Po dotarciu na miejsce i skorzystaniu z przydrożnego szaletu okazuje się na samym początku, że główna droga dojazdowa jest zablokowana i nie pozostaje mu nic innego, jak dostać się do miasta okrężną drogą, nie zważając na coraz gęstszą mgłę, której nie rozproszyłoby nawet najmocniejsze światło. Na drodze napotyka dziwne, zdeformowane, czyhające na jego życie potwory, lecz to nie one stanowią największe zagrożenie. Jedyni pozostali przy życiu ludzie zdają się żyć we własnym świecie, nosić swoje mniej, lub bardziej widoczne traumy i przywary, jednakże interakcje bohatera z nimi mają kluczowy wpływ na ich dalszy, nieunikniony los. Czy James odnajdzie swoją żonę? Kim jest tajemnicza postać, która zdaje się go prześladować podczas jego tułaczki? Czym tak naprawdę jest Silent Hill i jaką rolę w jego istnieniu odgrywa James? Tego dowiecie się, grając w Silent Hill 2 Remake.  Silent Hill 2 Remake jest opowiedzianą na nowo historią tragicznej wędrówki Jamesa Sunderlanda w poszukiwaniu jego zmarłej żony. Oryginał, który wydano w 2001 roku przez Konami i Team Silent, odświeżony został dzięki staraniom polskiego studia @blooberteam i współpracy artystów, którzy pracowali także przy oryginalnej wersji, jak chociażby Masahiro Ito, który przez lata tworzył do większości gier z tej serii kreacje potworów, świata przedstawionego w sposób, którego nie powstydziliby się nawet Beksiński, Giger i Bosch razem wzięci.  Jednakże miasto nie tylko przeraża wszechobecną, Kingowską mgłą, potworami z najgorszych koszmarów, lecz także atmosferą, budowaną przez budzącą napięcie muzykę, którą na nowo skomponował Arkadiusz Reikowski wraz z oryginalnym twórcą, Akirą Yamaoka. To dzięki niej każdy krok stawiany jest z nieufnością do tego, co może się pojawić za rogiem. W połączeniu z obrazem zmieniającego się i ulegającego deformacji miasteczka, lokacji, które pomagają Jamesowi stopniowo odkrywać prawdę o jego żonie, życiu i przywarach to właśnie muzyka czyni wędrówkę przerażającą i klimatyczną zarazem.  To emocjonalna, pełna suspensu podróż, ukazująca problematykę przem0cy psychicznej i fizycznej, nałogów, odrzucenia i wielu innych. Gra jest wręcz nafaszerowana ogromną ilością symboliki. Każde odwiedzone miejsce, każdy pokonany przeciwnik, postać, przedmiot czy wymagające zagadki mają swoje znaczenie. Mniej, lub bardziej oczywiste. Na końcu nasze poczynania rękami Jamesa zostaną osądzone w formie jednego z wielu zakończeń. Nie ulega wątpliwości, że każde z nich zapewni odpowiedni poziom emocji i pozostawi w głowie szereg ciężkich do odpowiedzenia pytań.  Silent Hill 2 Remake to nie jest zwyczajna gra z gatunku survival horror. To przede wszystkim wielowymiarowa interpretacja dzieł najwybitniejszych umysłów literackich i filmowych, wśród których dzieła Stephena Kinga, Deana Koontz’a, Davida Blocha, czy psychologiczne dreszczowce Davida Lyncha, to kropla w morzu inspiracji dla twórców gry, która od ponad dwóch dekad straszy graczy na całym świecie. Tylko, że w odświeżonej, pięknie wykonanej wersji. Dokładnie takiej, jaką sobie wyobrażałem przez 21 lat mojej miłości do wszystkich gier z serii Silent Hill. Takiej, która pierwszy raz wywołała we mnie prawdziwy strach (dzięki Ciapek), którego nigdy nie czułem grając w gry i czytając książki z gatunku grozy. Jako fan daję 999/10 i polecam każdemu.

Wife guy horror game (defo not lots of those around).  In all seriousness, amazing game all around.  Level design: this is where the game shines and brings most of its elements together. If you haven't played a Silent Hill game, think of it like a Resident Evil game (closest comparable example I can think of is RE2R). It's a lot about exploring paths and solving puzzles, all while threading through perilous paths and challenging encounters (all heightened by the spooky aspect of the game). Enemy placements never feel unfair (aside from a few challenging encounters towards the end, but they're meant to be hard), but do require situational awareness. Puzzles (and level progress) is always rewarding (it's never too cut and clear but neither too hard, while still requiring some fair brain power for some).  Story and themes: a refined version of the original (imo), and the original is well remembered for a reason. I can't really go into the story itself, but if you haven't played it, there are 2 questions that you should keep in mind: "What is Silent Hill (and its purpose)?" and "Why are the present people here?". It explores deep themes of psychology, while making good use of presentation through gameplay more so than cinematics (which makes it paying attention all the more rewarding, but it isn't the level of interpretation from Soulsborne games if you're worried). There's also some subtle choices the game never makes you aware of that dictate the end of the game (an important aspect is related to a key game mechanic, but it's up to you to guess), instead of having the obvious "choose your ending" options (although if you really don't want to screw yourself over you can always save at the end of the game, as there will be a "choice" before your final confrontation).  Gameplay: as previously mentioned, puzzles and map exploration are great (which is why I urge to not use guides, even when you struggle). The combat is probably the weak point of the game (although this doesn't mean it's bad). Melee never ever really changes throughout the game (you only need to learn a new enemy's attack pattern every so often), and it will most likely be your main recourse as standard enemies are pretty manageable and saving ammo for tough/boss encounters is vital. Gunplay is serviceable (standard third person shooting). However enemies are pretty fun to fight, and the diversity in how they attack you helps making combat fresh for every encounter (accentuated by the level design). Boss fights are also really great (one of which is probably amongst the best in terms of "what makes a good horror game boss fight?"). While your offensive capabilities are "simple" how they are used for which enemies and which scenarios is what makes combat good.  Art direction: one of the best in horror games. The soundtrack and sound design never misses. The world and levels are scary as they are enthralling. The otherworld (and fogworld) are still one of the most unique horror aesthetics conceived. They manage to perfectly capture the feelings of "you shouldn't be here" and "this place shouldn't exist". The environments are filled with gloominess and hopelessness, with shards of hope.  The horror: excellent. The main emotion felt is "uneasy" with certain high tension scenarios. It never goes for the jumpscares, but rather heavily relies on its suspense and slow built-up for the majority of the game, which makes the tense scenarios even more impactful when they do actually happen. The first quarter of the game is mostly used to introduce its world and workings, while the last quarter is where they bump up the horror aspect.

The first Silent Hill I've played and I really enjoyed it. I did have to play it in shortish chunks over a few weeks because I found the atmosphere so oppressive and unsettling that I couldn't do longer sessions. I think that is a testament to how effective Bloober team was at creating an affecting experience. The audio design was a highlight for me, score and SFX included. The pulsing stingers that would play during otherwise quiet moments really instilled dread in me any time I thought I was safe. The combat SFX was especially crunchy and I really liked the sound design for all the weapons. If you like the core gameplay of RE games and don't mind something with much less levity I'd check this one out.

First time playing a game from the series so hopefully this review serves as a barometer of sorts for those looking to break into the series. My experience was on a 4080 Super/13700k PC. As many reviews and news outlets have reported, the game suffers from consistent stuttering and hitching which depending on your sensitivity to that will possibly cause you to refund/uninstall or wait out hoping for Bloober to fix it (they won't and they kinda can't to some degree).   At first, I won't lie, it was really annoying to still deal with traversal stutter despite a shader compilation step and adding some mods that supposedly helped to further improve this via a guide here on Steam. I can't say for certain whether they really helped or not. I did not try playing without the mods to see if there was a change. I also did not play at release so it is hard for me to compare my experience to what apparently was an even worse one at launch. As of this time, there hasn't been a patch to the game in several months and like I mentioned above, Bloober will probably not fix this. To some degree, this is a UE5 issue that would require upgrading the engine version used. Newer versions of the engine have apparently added fixes to stuttering/hitching that we've all come to characterize as a fundamental part of playing a game using UE5. From what i've read/heard, this is not exactly easy nor inexpensive to do and so I doubt they will do so especially when they're already working on the remake for the first SH game. On top of that, they're probably also still doling out support for their newer game Chronos: The New Dawn.   To be very clear, I am not excusing this at all. I found it extremely annoying to have lurches while playing despite traversing areas that should have already had all their assets loaded/streamed in the first time. And that is still not acceptable on the first time as well when the shader compilation step is supposed to take care of that. A lot of the games being released now on UE5 all have these issues no matter if its a PC or console version and hence this is something that will only be fixed in time as devs use newer versions of UE5 that have somewhat tackled these engine-level issues. Is it true that devs also have a responsibility here? Definitely. But these recurring issues with UE5 are a problem with the engine itself more so than with developers using UE5.  Anyways, enough of UE5 stuttering issues. The only other visual oddity to me was the game's sort of mixed bag in terms of its presentation. What I mean here is that the game has a habit of both looking good and oddly bad at the same time. There's lots of aliasing, some environments look muddy and of lower quality than other sections in the game, the water was especially bad looking, etc.. Yet, I persisted.  So why did I persist and why am I ultimately recommending this game? Honestly, its because it does horror and atmosphere well which is what I wanted. There's a sort of surreal and dreamy quality as well as goofiness that often reminds me of Twin Peaks which I am huge fan of. There are twists you don't expect and terribly awful things that happen which depending on how you look at them, either help to villanize or endear characters to you. You feel empathy, pity, disgust, bewildered, etc at the various actions they take and their histories which slowly reveal themselves. The game seriously is a slow burn and this is what I hope you take away from the review the most, that if you continue you will be rewarded. I remember thinking about an hour and half in that I was gonna quit cause of the stuttering and the somewhat obtuse map system. The game is also a lot less hand-holdy than other more modern-horror games like the RE remakes.  The puzzles can be a bit confusing but they're definitely more interesting than those I've experienced. The enemies are grotesque, but they are not so oppressive and terrifying in comparison to the atmosphere, sound design, and the environments (despite their somewhat not visually appealing presentation). This is where the horror genre has to excel for me. The tension should be not facing the monsters, but the environment that has allowed them to exist and flourish in.  Again, the BIG TAKEAWAY here is that if you can get over the game's stuttering/mixed presentation is that the rest of the game really takes you on a journey dealing with themes of abuse, trauma, guilt, not belonging, anger, sadness, etc. The game deals with emotions and events that are deeply human and that paint the road to recovery as one marked with many mistakes, backtracking, and even maybe never actually recovering from the ordeal. I played this consistently once I got over my hump and I think that is solely because I wanted to keep going and experience more of the world and the sheer horror. Do yourself a favor,  play the game.
